> (`TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05`). Derived from the committed
> `sim_fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_m1_h10_knoise0_n500_batch_1_1000.qmd` with knob

> interval, so the MR (IJ) columns are unchanged; the field block is recorded
> alongside), an `fb_mode` knob (`"run"` computes FB in-replicate; `"join"`
> reads a committed FB bundle and joins by `sim_id`, never recomputing FB;
> `"none"` skips it), and a `campaign_tag` in the output stem so this template
> can never write into an existing stem (the h-tag is also widened to three
> digits, `h100`/`h175`, closing the `round(10*1.75) = round(10*1.8) = 18`
> collision). Every knob can be overridden per render through `FS_S7_*`
> environment variables (see @sec-setup), so batches run from ONE committed

> the pooled set.

# What this evaluates {#sec-intro}

**Multiplier resampling (MR)** (`fs_mr_inference()`, surfaced through
`forestsearch(mr_inference = TRUE)`) is a refit-free multiplier-bootstrap
approximation of León's post-selection bias correction, with an
infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) confidence interval. To first order its point
estimate equals León's Eq. 7 correction and its interval equals León's IJ
variance, the only approximation being the per-subgroup `dfbeta` linearization.

This document turns the single-trial validation into operating characteristics by
re-running the León (2024) estimation/coverage design and recording, **per
replicate on the same data and the same selected subgroup**:

* **oracle** $\hat\theta(H)$ — refit on the *true* harm subgroup;
* **naive** $\hat\theta(\hat H)$ — plugin on the identified subgroup;
* **FB** $\hat\theta^{*}(\hat H)$ — full nonparametric bootstrap
  bias-correction (`forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()`, León Eq. 7, the `H2`
  variant accounting for both bias sources) with its IJ interval;
* **MR** $\tilde\theta(\hat H)$ — refit-free multiplier resampling, holding the
  fitted candidate family fixed, with its IJ interval.

Each is compared to three truth targets: the per-replicate **oracle** estimate,
the controlled direct effect $\theta^{\ddagger}$ (CDE), and the marginal subgroup
hazard ratio $\theta^{\dagger}$. The two outputs are (1) the León Table-2-layout
estimation/coverage table with an MR block, and (2) the paired
FB$\leftrightarrow$MR agreement panel.  For `consistency` (a fixed
candidate family) that panel is the most direct empirical check of the
leading-order correspondence; for `dina`/`grf` the bootstrap regenerates the
family per resample, so the panel instead measures the family-regeneration gap
between the unconditional (FB) and conditional-on-family (MR) estimands.

The search runs under `consistency_method = "resample"` and
`sg_focus = "maxcons"` — the consistency argmax: highest consistency rate,
ties broken by effect. MR de-biases against that same candidate family, using
the rule `forestsearch()` derives from `sg_focus` rather than one set here, so
FB and MR share the same selection map. MR does not identify a subgroup; the
one reported is the one the search selected.

# The true subgroup {#sec-truth}

Everything below is scored against one planted region, so it is stated first.

**Definition.** $Q = \{\mathrm{er} \le 8\} \cap \{\mathrm{meno} = 0\}$ --- low
estrogen receptor **and** premenopausal. The `er` threshold is the 25th
percentile of the GBSG covariate template (er ranges 0--1144, median 36); the
`meno` term is the raw binary. The region covers **12.2%** of the template
(84 of 686 patients), and the DGM plants the harm effect there via
`setup_gbsg_dgm()`, which encodes it as `z1 = 1 & z3 = 1`.

**Why this region.** GBSG is a node-positive breast-cancer cohort, and
`er`/`meno` are the two covariates that jointly define endocrine
responsiveness: hormone-receptor status and menopausal status are the standard
axes on which adjuvant endocrine benefit is expected to differ. Planting harm
in the ER-low, premenopausal corner therefore makes the target clinically
coherent rather than an arbitrary covariate pair, and its ~12% prevalence puts
it in the small-subgroup regime that stresses the large-sample behaviour of the
correction --- which is the point of the exercise.

**What the search must do.** The analysis pool is the RAW covariates
(`er, age, meno, pgr, nodes, size, grade`); the pre-dichotomised `z1..z5` are
never supplied. The search has to rediscover both the variable pair and the
cut. `conf.cont_jcuts = list(er = 10)` deliberately replaces `er`'s default
cuts with a J-quantile grid at the $k/(J+1)$ quantiles --- `0, 3, 9, 17, 30,
44, 69.8, 100, 173.5, 293.7` --- which does **not** contain 8. The exact
boundary is therefore not on the grid and must be approximated. That is
deliberate: a design in which the true cut is a candidate hands the search the
answer.

**The near-tie this creates.** `age` correlates with `meno` strongly enough to
substitute for it, so the search can return $\{\mathrm{er}\} \cap
\{\mathrm{age}\}$ in place of $\{\mathrm{er}\} \cap \{\mathrm{meno}\}$ at
nearly equal fit. @sec-identification quantifies how often it does, and whether
more data resolves it.

# Endpoints, subgroups, and the harm convention {#sec-definitions}

**Endpoint.** `simulate_from_dgm()` emits a time-to-event pair: `y_sim` (the
event or censoring time, months) with indicator `event_sim`. Survival times come
from the AFT model fitted to the GBSG covariate template; censoring is Weibull,
scaled by `cens_adjust = log(1.5)`, with administrative censoring at
`analysis_time = 84` months. Treatment is `treat_sim`, randomised 1:1.

**Effect measure.** The Cox hazard ratio of treatment, estimated within a
region by `coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim)`. Model SEs
(`*_se` columns) are on the **log**-hazard-ratio scale while point estimates
and interval bounds are on the **HR** scale; the estimation table reports
$\text{SD}_{\beta}$ and $\widehat{\text{SD}}_{\beta}$ on the log scale and
hides the HR-scale twins.

**Harm.** On a hazard ratio, larger is worse: $\text{HR} > 1$ means treatment
raises the hazard, so **harm is HR > 1** and the null is HR = 1. Nothing is
re-oriented on this path --- every estimator column, every interval bound, and
every target is on the natural HR scale as fitted. (The continuous twin *does*
re-orient, because its raw scale runs the other way; see its matching section.)

**The three regions.**

* $Q$ --- the **true** planted region, $\{\mathrm{er} \le 8\} \cap
  \{\mathrm{meno} = 0\}$, known to the DGM and carried per subject as
  `flag_harm`. Fixed across replicates. Defined and motivated in @sec-truth.
* $\widehat H$ --- the **realized** region: whatever rule the search returned on
  this replicate, recorded as `sg_def`. Varies replicate to replicate, and is
  the region the naive, FB and MR estimators are computed on. Membership is
  `treat.recommend == 0`.
* $\widehat H^{c}$ --- its complement within the trial, `treat.recommend == 1`.

The **oracle** is the only estimator fitted on $Q$; naive, FB and MR are all
fitted on $\widehat H$. That is why the oracle's meaningful comparisons are
against the true-region targets and not against $\beta(\widehat H)$.

**The four targets** each estimator is scored against, in the notation the
estimation table uses: $\hat\theta(H)$ the per-replicate oracle; $\beta(\widehat
H)$ the population effect at the *realized* region (the Theorem 2 target, and
the only one that moves with $\widehat H$); $\theta^{\ddagger}$ the CDE at $Q$;
and $\theta^{\dagger}$ the marginal effect at $Q$. The last two differ here
because the hazard ratio is non-collapsible.

## How "MR flags harm in x%" is computed {#sec-mr-harm}

The estimation-table footnote reports the share of replicates in which MR
**confirms** harm. That is a decision, not an estimate, and it is separate from
the interval: it asks whether the *de-biased* effect still points at harm after
the selection correction, which is exactly the question the naive estimate
cannot answer.

**The rule.** `fs_mr_inference()` de-biases the naive subgroup effect, then
applies one comparison on the working scale
(`fs_mr_inference.R`):

```
t_cmp    <- if (log_scale) log(t_confirm) else t_confirm
ci_lo_1s <- beta_deb - qnorm(0.95) * se
flag     <- if (confirm_rule == "point") (beta_deb >= t_cmp)
            else                          (ci_lo_1s >= t_cmp)
```

`beta_deb` is the de-biased estimate and `se` the interval SE (the IJ SE under
`ci_method = "ij"`). So `"point"` asks whether the de-biased **point estimate**
clears the threshold, and `"ci"` asks whether the one-sided 95%
selection-adjusted **lower bound** does --- strictly the more conservative of
the two. The result is `harm_flag`, surfaced on the fitted object as
`mr_harm_confirmed` and recorded here as `mr_harm_flag`.

**The threshold, and why it sits at the null.** On this path the effect measure is the hazard ratio, so the working
scale is the **log** scale and `t_confirm` is compared as `log(t_confirm)`.
Leaving `mr_t_confirm = NULL` takes the package's near-null default,
`t_confirm = 1` for ratio measures, so by default the question is
"is the de-biased hazard ratio still at or above 1?" --- *not* whether it still clears the screening
threshold used during the search. That distinction is deliberate and
`fs_mr_inference()` documents the reason: the de-biasing correction over-shrinks
true effects, so testing against a screening-level threshold would reject
genuine subgroups. Raising it to, say, `mr_t_confirm <- 1.10` would demand a de-biased HR of
at least 1.10 before harm is called.

**Three-valued, and why that matters for the percentage.** `harm_flag` is
`TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NA`, the last when MR ran but bailed before it could
compute one. The package documentation is explicit that `NA` here is *absence
of evidence, not evidence against harm*, and warns against `isTRUE()`, which
collapses `NA` to `FALSE`. This document records the flag three-valued and the
reported percentage is `mean(..., na.rm = TRUE)`, so those replicates leave the
denominator rather than entering it as "harm not confirmed".

**Controlling it.** Both settings are knobs in @sec-setup --- `mr_t_confirm`
and `mr_confirm_rule` --- assembled into `mr_inference_args` and passed to
`forestsearch(mr_inference_args = ...)`. `mr_t_confirm` is on the **effect**
scale, not the working log scale; the code takes the log internally for ratio
measures. The settings actually used are echoed in @sec-counts, after the run, so what
is reported is what was used rather than what was intended.


# Setup — all knobs {#sec-setup}

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.t0_doc <- Sys.time()    # start of document-level wall-clock (total reported at the very end)

# NOTE: forestsearch must be INSTALLED (devtools::install()), not load_all():
# the doFuture multisession workers spawn separate R processes that only see the
# installed package.
library(forestsearch)
library(survival)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(foreach)
library(doFuture)
library(future)

# Parallelization topology (works with run_mode / batching above):
#   "sims"  -> replicates fan out across workers; each replicate's forestsearch +
#              bootstrap run sequentially.  Best when n_sims >= n_workers (fills cores).
#   "boots" -> replicates run sequentially; the forestsearch search AND the nb_boots
#              bootstrap fan out across workers WITHIN each replicate.  Best when
#              n_sims is small (single-/few-trial deep dives) and "sims" would idle cores.
# Bootstrap resample indices are seeded on the main process, so results are
# plan-invariant: the two modes differ in WALL-CLOCK only, not in detection/estimates.
parallel_mode <- "sims"

# ── Environment overrides (FS_S7_*) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# ONE committed file runs every batch: each knob below reads an FS_S7_* env var
# first and falls back to the in-file default, so an unattended driver renders
#   FS_S7_HR=1.75 FS_S7_START=1001 FS_S7_NSIMS=1000 FS_S7_FB=none \
#     quarto render sim_fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_field_m1_template.qmd --output ...
# without ever editing the committed template.  Every resolved value is echoed
# below and lands in the bundle's meta, so a render is auditable from its
# output alone.
.env_chr <- function(k, d) { v <- Sys.getenv(k, unset = NA); if (is.na(v) || !nzchar(v)) d else v }
.env_int <- function(k, d) as.integer(.env_chr(k, d))
.env_num <- function(k, d) as.numeric(.env_chr(k, d))

# ── Counts (the only knobs to change for production) ───────────────────────
n_sims       <- .env_int("FS_S7_NSIMS", 1000L)   # simulated trials per batch
diag_mode    <- FALSE     # DIAGNOSTIC: TRUE caps the run to 5 replicates and relays each
                          # worker's forestsearch() error (otherwise swallowed by the inner
                          # tryCatch).  Set FALSE for a real run.
# fb_mode governs the FB comparator (decision F5 of the task):
#   "run"  -> compute FB in-replicate (nb_boots below must be >= 1)
#   "join" -> NEVER recompute FB: read the committed FB bundle at fb_join_path
#             and join its fb_* columns by sim_id after the run loop.  sim_ids
#             outside the bundle simply stay NA (recorded as FB-absent).
#   "none" -> no FB at all.
fb_mode      <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FB", "none")     # "run" | "join" | "none"
stopifnot(fb_mode %in% c("run", "join", "none"))
fb_join_path <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FB_PATH",
  "results/fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_m1_h10_knoise0_n500_combined_1_500.rds")
# GATE 2 AMENDMENT (Larry, 2026-09-05, Stage 2 STOP resolution -- the
# authorized one-knob change): enumerated cross-vintage selection-flip
# replicates.  The committed h10 bundles (forestsearch 0.2.0/0.2.1) and the
# current package (0.3.5) select a different near-tie rule on exactly these
# sim_ids (REPORT_mr_field_s7_stage2_2026-09-05.md: sims 393, 780; data and
# oracle identical, selection flips at the consistency screen).  The FB-join
# identity assertion still STOPS on any replicate NOT in this list; listed
# replicates are skipped -- never joined, recorded FB-absent -- with both
# selections (committed and fresh) printed.  Recorded in meta.  h175 has no
# flips; the list is inert there (fb_mode is never "join" for h175).
fb_join_skip <- local({
  v <- .env_chr("FS_S7_JOIN_SKIP", "393,780")
  if (nzchar(v)) sort(unique(as.integer(strsplit(v, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))) else integer(0)
})
nb_boots     <- if (identical(fb_mode, "run")) .env_int("FS_S7_NB_BOOTS", 300L) else 0L
k_random_noise <- .env_int("FS_S7_KNOISE", 0L)   # Add k_random_noise confounders

# ── Batching across renders (split one long run into seed-disjoint pieces) ──
# Each render is ONE batch of `n_sims` replicates starting at `sim_id_start`.
# Every per-replicate seed is `seed_base + sim_id` (DGM, search, bootstrap, AND
# the noise covariates), so disjoint sim_id ranges across renders are independent
# and pool to exactly what one big run would have produced:
#
#   Batch 1 : run_mode "batch", sim_id_start = 1     -> ..._res_1_100.rds
#   Batch 2 : run_mode "batch", sim_id_start = 101   -> ..._res_101_200.rds   (re-render)
#   ...      (re-render per batch, advancing sim_id_start by n_sims each time)
#   Combine : run_mode "combine"                     -> reads ..._res_*.rds, rbinds,
#                                                       renders every table on the union
#
# DEFAULT is a single batch starting at 1: render once and you have the whole run.
run_mode     <- .env_chr("FS_S7_MODE", "batch")   # "batch" (run + save one piece) | "combine" (merge + report)
sim_id_start <- .env_int("FS_S7_START", 1L)       # first sim_id of THIS batch (1001L, ... for later pieces)

# ── The identifier: engine + focus ─────────────────────────────────────────
# These two together ARE the estimator, and both feed the output stem below,
# so they are defined here rather than with the search-tuning knobs.  Defining
# sg_focus later would leave focus_tag undefined at stem-construction time.
subgroup_method <- "consistency"  # "consistency" | "dina" | "grf"
sg_focus           <- "maxeffCons" # consistency argmax: highest effect meeting consistency rate,
                                   # ties broken by subgroup size

target_hr_harm  <- .env_num("FS_S7_HR", 1.0)   # calibrate k_inter to this Cox HR in the harm subgroup
n_sample        <- .env_int("FS_S7_N", 500L)   # M1 sample size

# Output stem derives from the knobs above, so changing n_sample / target_hr_harm /
# k_random_noise / subgroup_method / sg_focus renames every saved file automatically
# -- no manual edit, and runs under a different engine or focus never overwrite each
# other. The leading token IS the subgroup method: "fs" for consistency, else
# "dina"/"grf"; focus_tag follows it. Batch range is appended below.
#
# NOT back-compatible: the stem changed from "<engine>_t1_t2_m1_..." to
# "<engine>_<focus>_fb_mr_m1_...".  Batch .rds files written under the old stem
# are invisible to combine_glob -- re-run them or rename them to match.
method_tag   <- if (identical(subgroup_method, "consistency")) "fs" else subgroup_method

# The IDENTIFIER is the estimator here; FB and MR are resampling procedures applied
# to it.  The identifier has two parts -- the engine (method_tag) and the selection
# focus -- and only the engine was in the stem, so re-running a cell under a
# different sg_focus silently overwrote the same .rds, and combine_glob pooled the
# two together.  focus_tag closes that.
#
# Aliases normalize FORWARD to the descriptive name rather than back through
# .normalize_sg_focus(), which maps eff -> "hr": the Cox-flavoured internal
# vocabulary.  "eff*" generalizes across GLM outcomes, "hr" does not.
# Fold every alias pair onto one tag.  .normalize_sg_focus() collapses three
# pairs -- eff/hr, effMaxSG/hrMaxSG, effMinSG/hrMinSG -- so each pair is one
# rule under two spellings.  Without folding, identical runs written under
# different spellings land in different stems and never pool.  The eff*
# spelling wins because it carries over to GLM outcomes; the consistency
# argmax takes "maxcons", which names what the rule does.
# One source of truth: fs_focus_tag() holds the (subgroup_method, sg_focus)
# -> stem tag map for every driver.  It was pasted into each one and drifted;
# the method-blind copies tagged DINA/GRF runs with the consistency name for a
# rule those engines never ran.
focus_tag <- forestsearch::fs_focus_tag(subgroup_method, sg_focus)
if (!identical(focus_tag, sg_focus))
  cat(sprintf("NOTE: sg_focus '%s' is an alias on the %s path; output stem uses focus tag '%s'.
",
              sg_focus, subgroup_method, focus_tag))

# TEMPLATE STEM (three deliberate departures from the parent document, all
# collision guards per Gate 0 finding 2 of TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05):
#   1. the token is "fb_mr_field", so no template output can ever glob-match
#      the committed fb_mr / mr stems;
#   2. the h-tag is THREE digits from round(100 * hr) -- h100, h175 -- closing
#      the parent's round(10*1.75) = round(10*1.8) = "h18" collision;
#   3. a mandatory campaign_tag suffix namespaces every campaign (smoke vs
#      production vs any rerun), so combine_glob can never pool across them.
campaign_tag <- .env_chr("FS_S7_CAMPAIGN", "c1")
stopifnot(grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9]+$", campaign_tag))
rds_stem     <- sprintf("%s_%s_fb_mr_field_m1_h%03d_knoise%d_n%d_%s",
                        method_tag, focus_tag, round(100 * target_hr_harm),
                        k_random_noise, n_sample, campaign_tag)

# ADOPTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN: quick-run stem tagging.
# Without this a smoke render (nb_boots = 10, n_sims = 20) writes to the SAME
# stem as a production batch, and combine_glob then pools the two silently --
# a handful of B = 10 replicates averaged in with B = 300 ones, with nothing in
# the pooled bundle recording that it happened.  Tagging the stem puts quick
# runs in a namespace combine can never match.  Set FALSE for production.
# (campaign_tag above already namespaces campaigns; quickrun is kept as a
# second, orthogonal guard for ad-hoc smoke renders inside a campaign.)
quickrun     <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_QUICKRUN", "FALSE"), "TRUE")
if (isTRUE(quickrun)) rds_stem <- paste0(rds_stem, "_quickrun")

sim_id_end   <- sim_id_start + n_sims - 1L
rds_path     <- file.path("results", sprintf("%s_res_%d_%d.rds", rds_stem, sim_id_start, sim_id_end))  # THIS batch's file
combine_glob <- file.path("results", sprintf("%s_res_*.rds", rds_stem))   # combine mode: which batch files to merge
combine_files <- NULL   # optional explicit character vector; NULL -> use combine_glob
# FS_S7_SAVE_COMBINED=FALSE lets a verification combine render run every
# table WITHOUT rewriting an already-committed pooled bundle (the committed
# bundles are read-only inputs; TASK_bias_coverage_display_2026-09-06).
save_combined <- !identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_SAVE_COMBINED", "TRUE"), "FALSE")   # combine mode: ALSO write the pooled bundle to disk
combined_path <- NULL   # NULL -> auto "results/<rds_stem>_combined_<min>_<max>.rds" (deliberately
                        # outside combine_glob, so a re-combine never re-ingests the pool)

# ── Persist results? The FB bootstrap (B x n_sims, each re-running the
# engine) is the wall-clock bottleneck; saving the results bundle lets you
# regenerate the summary tables without re-running the simulation. 

# Scale-up scenarios for the timing projection (n_sims, nb_boots). Edit freely.
proj_scenarios <- list(
  c(n_sims = 100L,  nb_boots = 300L),
  c(n_sims = 500L,  nb_boots = 300L),
  c(n_sims = 10000L, nb_boots = 500L)
)
                          # the MR -- see run_fb below.
mr_draws   <- 5000L     # MR multiplier draws         (keep ~2000)

save_rds <- identical(run_mode, "batch") && !is.null(rds_path)  # write only when running a batch

# FB is the wall-clock bottleneck.  forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() itself
# requires nb_boots >= 1 (it errors otherwise), so a skip is enforced HERE -- the
# bootstrap is simply never called -- rather than by passing 0L/NULL into it.
# nb_boots = 0L (or NULL) => run_fb = FALSE => MR-only run.
run_fb <- is.numeric(nb_boots) && length(nb_boots) == 1L && nb_boots >= 1L
run_smoke    <- TRUE      # master flag; FALSE short-circuits the run loop


# ── DGM: León M1 cell (GBSG AFT super-population, alt hypothesis) ───────────
dgm_model       <- "alt"
analysis_time   <- 84     # administrative censoring (months)
cens_adjust     <- log(1.5)
n_super         <- 100000L  # fixed super-population = the eligible-patient universe; trials AND beta(Hhat) draw from this one pool

# ── Subgroup-identification method ─────────────────────────────────────────
# The FB bootstrap (H2, León Eq.7) re-runs whichever engine fs.est used,
# regenerating the candidate family on each resample, so the FB-vs-MR
# comparison is produced for every engine.  Interpretation differs by engine:
# for "consistency" the family is fixed, so FB and MR target the same
# estimand and should agree (the dfbeta-linearisation check); for "dina"/"grf"
# the family regenerates per resample, so FB is the *unconditional*
# comparator against MR's *conditional-on-family* estimate, and a
# FB<->MR gap is the family-regeneration signal, not an error.

grf_selection   <- "frontier"      # only if subgroup_method == "grf": "tree" | "frontier"
grf_select_statistic <- "effect"   # only if grf frontier: "dr" | "effect" (no-op for tree)
grf_depth       <- 2L              # GRF policy-tree depth / max frontier conjunctions
dmin.grf        <- 0.0             # GRF DR-score screening floor
dina_args       <- list()          # extra args forwarded to the DINA selector (dina_args =)
dina_select_statistic <- "effect"  # only if subgroup_method == "dina": "dina" | "effect"

# ── Search configuration (León tuning; resample identification) ────────────
# sg_focus and subgroup_method are set earlier, with the output stem they feed.
consistency_method <- "resample"   # decided: resample identification (the new default)
# MR's de-biasing rule is no longer set explicitly: forestsearch() derives it from
# sg_focus ("maxcons" for the consistency engine), reproducing the legacy
# value while staying faithful per engine.  Override via `reselection =` in
# mr_inference_args (advanced use only).
selection_rule     <- "neighborhood"  # effMaxSG/effMinSG band rule.  INERT under
                                      # sg_focus = "maxcons", whose key is
                                      # consistency-primary with no band term.
                                      # Retained unchanged so the effMaxSG/effMinSG
                                      # arms can use it.
stop_threshold     <- NULL            # early stopping.  NULL is what this config
                                      # already resolves to: forestsearch() resets
                                      # it for the canonical "hr" family, which
                                      # "maxcons" normalizes to, and does so WITHOUT
                                      # warning unless supplied explicitly.  Named
                                      # here so the setting is inspectable.
effect_neighborhood <- 0.10           # package default; band half-width for
                                      # effMaxSG/effMinSG.  Pinned rather than
                                      # inherited so the value is visible; inert
                                      # under sg_focus = "maxcons".
hr_threshold       <- 0.90
hr_consistency     <- 0.80
pconsistency       <- 0.90
fs_splits          <- 400L         # moot under "resample" (closed-form, not literal split)
maxk               <- 2L
n_min              <- NULL
d0_min             <- 10L
d1_min             <- 10L
# RESTORED (were commented out): the consistency `method_args` block below
# references all three UNCONDITIONALLY, and it is built OUTSIDE the tryCatch
# around forestsearch(), so a missing symbol here escaped as an error from
# record_replicate() itself.  Every replicate was then dropped
# (.errorhandling = "remove" in "sims" mode, the outer tryCatch in "boots"),
# leaving results = NULL -- a configuration failure reading as a scientific
# null, and surfacing ~400 lines later as "incorrect number of dimensions".
# Values are the package defaults and match the committed MD harness.
use_lasso          <- FALSE
use_dina           <- FALSE
use_grf            <- FALSE         # FALSE = LASSO-only (fast, "FSl"); set TRUE for "FSlg"
use_twostage       <- TRUE

fs_conf_force      <- c("meno == 0", "er <= 0", "pgr <= 0")   # premenopausal (raw analog of z3 == 1)
fs_conf.cont_jcuts <- list(er = 10)     # J-quantile grid on raw ER (analog of z1; now meaningful, ER is continuous)

# ── MR inference controls (mr_inference_args) ───────────────────────────────
# Exposed as explicit knobs rather than an inline list, so the harm-confirmation
# rule is visible and changeable.  See @sec-definitions for what these do.
#
#   mr_t_confirm    Harm-confirmation threshold on the EFFECT scale (not the
#                   working log scale).  NULL uses the package's near-null
#                   default: 1 for ratio measures (HR/OR/RR/IRR), 0 for
#                   differences (MD/RD).  Set it NEAR THE NULL rather than at
#                   the screening threshold -- fs_mr_inference()'s own
#                   documentation warns that the de-biasing correction
#                   over-shrinks true effects, so a screening-level threshold
#                   would reject genuine subgroups.
#   mr_confirm_rule "point" tests the de-biased point estimate against
#                   t_confirm; "ci" tests the one-sided 95% selection-adjusted
#                   LOWER bound and is therefore strictly more conservative.
# THE task's knob delta: ci_method = "field".  fs_mr_inference() computes
# everything the "ij" path computes -- the debiased element keeps the IJ
# interval, so the mr_* (IJ) recorder columns are IDENTICAL to an "ij" run --
# and additionally returns the field-calibrated block (fit$mr_inference$field),
# recorded below as the fld_H_* columns.  The field's Monte Carlo sizes
# field_R_out/field_R_in are NOT forwarded by forestsearch() (Stage 0 report,
# finding under 0a), so the package defaults 1000/500 apply; decision F4 of the
# task pins those defaults for this study.
mr_ci_method    <- "field"    # "ij" | "wald" | "field"
mr_t_confirm    <- NULL       # NULL -> near-null default for this measure
mr_confirm_rule <- "point"    # "point" | "ci"
# Uniform (kappa) calibration knob (TASK_mr_field_uniform_2026-09-05): when
# TRUE the gate additionally runs the kappa(Sigma-hat) sweep and the recorder
# captures the fld_H_kappa/... columns below.  FALSE leaves every output
# byte-identical to a pre-uniform render (add-only, default off).
mr_field_uniform <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_UNIFORM", "FALSE"), "TRUE")

# t_confirm is omitted from the list when NULL so the package resolves its own
# measure-aware default rather than receiving an explicit NULL.
mr_inference_args <- c(
  list(ci_method = mr_ci_method, draws = mr_draws, include_complement = TRUE,
       confirm_rule = mr_confirm_rule, field_uniform = mr_field_uniform),
  if (!is.null(mr_t_confirm)) list(t_confirm = mr_t_confirm))

# ── Column names emitted by simulate_from_dgm() ────────────────────────────
outcome_name   <- "y_sim"
event_name     <- "event_sim"
treat_name     <- "treat_sim"
id_name        <- "id"
harm_col       <- "flag_harm"
# Raw GBSG covariate candidates (as in a real analysis): forestsearch discovers
# its own cuts. Continuous -> er, age, pgr, nodes, size; categorical -> meno (0/1),
# grade (1/2/3). The pre-dichotomized z1..z5 are NOT used. The true harm subgroup
# (er <= 25th pct & meno == 0) must be re-discovered from these raw variables.

confounders_base <- c("er", "age", "meno", "pgr", "nodes", "size", "grade")

# ── Reproducibility / parallelism ──────────────────────────────────────────
seed_base  <- 8316951L
# ~60 workers is this study's target concurrency (task 1c: the host is
# memory-bandwidth-bound for these runs; 120 workers gained nothing on
# 2026-09-05).  Overridable per render, capped at physical cores - 1.
n_workers  <- min(.env_int("FS_S7_WORKERS", 60L),
                  max(1L, parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) - 1L))

stopifnot(parallel_mode %in% c("sims", "boots"))
inner_parallel <- if (identical(parallel_mode, "boots"))
  list(plan = "multisession", workers = n_workers) else list(plan = "sequential")
cat(sprintf("Parallel mode: %s (%s)\n", parallel_mode,
            if (identical(parallel_mode, "boots")) "replicates sequential, bootstrap parallel"
            else "replicates parallel, bootstrap sequential"))
z975       <- qnorm(0.975)

cat(sprintf("Run config: method=%s%s, n_sims=%d, nb_boots=%s, mr_draws=%d, workers=%d\n",
            subgroup_method,
            if (identical(subgroup_method, "grf")) paste0("/", grf_selection) else "",
            n_sims, if (is.null(nb_boots)) "0 (skip)" else as.character(nb_boots),
            mr_draws, n_workers))
# Resolved template knobs -- the render's audit line (env overrides included).
cat(sprintf("Template knobs: hr=%.2f n=%d ci_method=%s uniform=%s fb_mode=%s campaign=%s run_mode=%s sim_id %d-%d quickrun=%s\n",
            target_hr_harm, n_sample, mr_ci_method, mr_field_uniform, fb_mode, campaign_tag,
            run_mode, sim_id_start, sim_id_start + n_sims - 1L, quickrun))
cat(sprintf("Output stem: %s\n", rds_stem))
```

# Build the DGM and read off the truth targets

```{r build-dgm}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0 || all(is.na(a))) b else a

if (identical(run_mode, "batch")) {
  k_inter <- calibrate_k_inter(target_hr_harm = target_hr_harm,
                               model = dgm_model, use_ahr = FALSE)

  dgm <- setup_gbsg_dgm(model = dgm_model, k_inter = k_inter,
                        n_super = n_super, seed = seed_base)
  dgm <- compute_dgm_cde(dgm)   # attaches CDE (theta-ddagger) targets

  # Fixed (population) truth targets, read defensively from the DGM object.
  truth <- list(
    hr_causal   = dgm$hr_causal   %||% NA_real_,                 # overall causal HR
    marg_H      = dgm$hr_H_true   %||% NA_real_,                 # theta-dagger (H)
    marg_Hc     = dgm$hr_Hc_true  %||% NA_real_,                 # theta-dagger (Hc)
    cde_H       = dgm$cde_H       %||% (dgm$hazard_ratios$CDE_harm    %||% NA_real_),  # theta-ddagger (H)
    cde_Hc      = dgm$cde_Hc      %||% (dgm$hazard_ratios$CDE_no_harm %||% NA_real_)   # theta-ddagger (Hc)
  )

  cat("DGM truth targets (population):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  overall causal HR      : %.3f\n", truth$hr_causal))
  cat(sprintf("  theta-dagger  H / Hc   : %.3f / %.3f\n", truth$marg_H, truth$marg_Hc))
  cat(sprintf("  theta-ddagger H / Hc   : %.3f / %.3f\n", truth$cde_H,  truth$cde_Hc))

  # Conditional target beta(Hhat) is evaluated on the ENTIRE super-population
  # (every dgm$df_super subject once) -- the SAME fixed universe the trials
  # sub-sample -- under the trials' randomized, censored analysis.  beta(Hhat) is
  # n-invariant (a property of the realized rule and the population).  The sanity
  # MR recomputes theta-dagger on this same frame at the true harm flag; it
  # should reproduce dgm$hr_H_true / hr_Hc_true, confirming "population" reads.
  # API ALIGNMENT: the eval-frame / theta-dagger helpers were renamed under the
  # unified betaHhat truth layer (R/betaHhat_truth.R) and now dispatch on
  # outcome_type: build_eval_frame() -> fs_build_eval_frame() and
  # betaHhat_theta_dagger_check() -> fs_betaHhat_theta_dagger_check().  Same
  # survival construction (full super-population, each subject once), so the
  # numbers are unchanged; the survival-only knobs analysis_time/cens_adjust are
  # still accepted on this path.
  eval_df <- fs_build_eval_frame(dgm, outcome_type = "survival",
                                 eval_seed = 20260628L,
                                 analysis_time = analysis_time,
                                 cens_adjust = cens_adjust)
  .td_chk <- fs_betaHhat_theta_dagger_check(eval_df, outcome_type = "survival",
                                            harm.name = harm_col,
                                            outcome.name = outcome_name,
                                            event.name = event_name,
                                            treat.name = treat_name)
  cat(sprintf("  beta(Hhat) eval frame  : n=%d (FULL super-population, each subject once; eval_seed = 20260628)\n", nrow(eval_df)))
  cat(sprintf("  theta-dagger (on frame): %.3f / %.3f  (cross-check vs above)\n",
              .td_chk[["thetaDagger_H"]], .td_chk[["thetaDagger_Hc"]]))
} else {
  # combine mode: the DGM is not needed here; truth is read from the batch
  # bundles in the combine step below.
  truth <- NULL
  cat("Combine mode: DGM build skipped (truth read from batch files).\n")
}
```

# Per-replicate paired recorder

For each simulated trial: identify $\hat H$ and obtain the naive + MR in
one `forestsearch()` call, run the FB bootstrap on the *same* fit (inheriting
`consistency_method = "resample"`), and refit the oracle on the true subgroup.
Inner `forestsearch()`/bootstrap parallelism follows `parallel_mode` (@sec-setup):
in `"sims"` mode it is sequential because the outer loop parallelises across trials;
in `"boots"` mode the outer loop is sequential and the search + bootstrap parallelise
across workers within each trial.  Results are identical either way.

```{r recorder}
# Cox HR + delta-method 95% CI on a subset (for the per-replicate oracle).
# Guards against separation: non-finite coef/SE (the "coefficient may be
# infinite" case) returns a clean NA triple rather than Inf/NaN bounds.
.cox_hr_ci <- function(df) {
  if (sum(df[[event_name]]) < 5L || length(unique(df[[treat_name]])) < 2L)
    return(c(est = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, se = NA_real_))
  fml <- stats::as.formula(
    sprintf("survival::Surv(%s, %s) ~ %s", outcome_name, event_name, treat_name))
  fit <- tryCatch(survival::coxph(fml, data = df), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(c(est = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, se = NA_real_))
  b  <- unname(stats::coef(fit)[1])
  v  <- unname(suppressWarnings(diag(stats::vcov(fit))[1]))  # unname: else lo/hi inherit coef name -> oH["lo"] = NA
  se <- if (is.finite(v) && v > 0) sqrt(v) else NA_real_
  if (!is.finite(b) || !is.finite(se))
    return(c(est = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, se = NA_real_))
  c(est = exp(b), lo = exp(b - z975 * se), hi = exp(b + z975 * se), se = se)
}

# Recover the log-HR (beta-scale) SE from an HR-scale SD: sd_hr = HR * se_beta,
# so se_beta = sd_hr / HR.  Used for the FB row, whose bootstrap summary reports
# sdH2 on the HR scale.  Returns NA on a non-positive/non-finite estimate.
.se_beta_hr <- function(sd_hr, hr) {
  if (is.finite(sd_hr) && is.finite(hr) && hr > 0) sd_hr / hr else NA_real_
}

# rule_covs(): the variable names appearing in a realized rule (for the
# identification figures).  NOT a package export -- the survival template
# sourced it from a working-directory helper that is absent here, which is why
# `rec$covs` below raised "could not find function rule_covs".  Defined inline
# over the package internal .fs_rule_columns() (the same wrapper the continuous
# twin uses); fs.est$sg.harm is a character vector of rule terms, which
# .fs_rule_columns() parses across "&"/"|" and strips the comparison operators.
rule_covs <- function(rule) forestsearch:::.fs_rule_columns(rule)

# Classification of the identified subgroup against the true harm flag.
# sg_hat is grp.consistency$sg.harm.id: a per-subject 0/1 vector, length
# nrow(df), aligned to the input rows (clean on the consistency result; the
# GRF-object naming collision does not apply here).
.classify <- function(sg_hat, truth) {
  out <- c(sens = NA_real_, spec = NA_real_, ppv = NA_real_, npv = NA_real_)
  if (is.null(sg_hat) || length(sg_hat) != length(truth)) return(out)
  sg_hat <- as.integer(sg_hat); truth <- as.integer(truth)
  tp <- sum(sg_hat == 1 & truth == 1); fp <- sum(sg_hat == 1 & truth == 0)
  fn <- sum(sg_hat == 0 & truth == 1); tn <- sum(sg_hat == 0 & truth == 0)
  out["sens"] <- if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else NA_real_
  out["spec"] <- if (tn + fp > 0) tn / (tn + fp) else NA_real_
  out["ppv"]  <- if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else NA_real_
  out["npv"]  <- if (tn + fn > 0) tn / (tn + fn) else NA_real_
  out
}

# One all-NA record (returned on failure so the loop never aborts a cell).
.na_record <- function(sim_id) data.frame(
  sim_id = sim_id, detected = 0L, mr_ok = 0L, n_sel = NA_integer_,
  # ADOPTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN: the CONFIG-ERROR / NO-DETECTION /
  # DETECTED trichotomy.  `detected` alone cannot distinguish "the search ran
  # and found nothing" from "the replicate never got that far", so a broken
  # configuration reads as a scientific null in every downstream rate.  Set at
  # each exit point below, and by .safe_record() when the replicate itself
  # errors.
  status = NA_character_,
  n_harm = NA_integer_, n_true = NA_integer_,
  label = NA_character_, sg_def = NA_character_, covs = NA_character_,
  err_msg = NA_character_,   # populated by .safe_record() on a replicate-level
                             # error, so a CONFIG failure is visible in the
                             # bundle instead of vanishing into a dropped row
                             # (the md40 harness's CONFIG-ERROR arm).
  betaHhat_H = NA_real_, betaHhat_Hc = NA_real_,
  fb_secs = NA_real_, fit_mr_secs = NA_real_, fb_err = NA_character_,
  or_H_est = NA, or_H_lo = NA, or_H_hi = NA, or_H_se = NA,
  or_Hc_est = NA, or_Hc_lo = NA, or_Hc_hi = NA, or_Hc_se = NA,
  nv_H_est = NA, nv_H_lo = NA, nv_H_hi = NA, nv_H_se = NA,
  nv_Hc_est = NA, nv_Hc_lo = NA, nv_Hc_hi = NA, nv_Hc_se = NA,
  fb_H_est = NA, fb_H_lo = NA, fb_H_hi = NA, fb_H_se = NA,
  fb_Hc_est = NA, fb_Hc_lo = NA, fb_Hc_hi = NA, fb_Hc_se = NA,
  mr_H_est = NA, mr_H_lo = NA, mr_H_hi = NA, mr_H_se_ij = NA,
  mr_Hc_est = NA, mr_Hc_lo = NA, mr_Hc_hi = NA, mr_Hc_se_ij = NA,
  # MR (field) block, Hhat ONLY (decision F3: the gate computes no field for
  # the complement; Hhat^c stays on the IJ interval above).  Scales follow the
  # gate's return: est2 and the interval bounds are to_eff()'d (HR scale, like
  # every other *_est/lo/hi column); lambda_mean / lambda_sd (= se_field) and
  # the seven lambda quantiles are RAW log-HR-scale Monte Carlo summaries.
  fld_H_est2 = NA_real_,                                   # two-term shrunk-field estimate
  fld_H_lo2s = NA_real_, fld_H_hi2s = NA_real_,            # two-sided 95% quantile interval (primary, F4)
  fld_H_lo1s = NA_real_,                                   # one-sided 95% lower bound (supplementary)
  fld_H_lo_se = NA_real_, fld_H_hi_se = NA_real_,          # SE-type interval: est2 -+ z * lambda_sd
  fld_H_se = NA_real_,                                     # se_field = lambda_sd (log-HR scale)
  fld_H_lam_mean = NA_real_,                               # mean Lambda* (log-HR scale)
  fld_H_q05 = NA_real_, fld_H_q25 = NA_real_, fld_H_q50 = NA_real_,
  fld_H_q75 = NA_real_, fld_H_q95 = NA_real_,
  fld_H_q025 = NA_real_, fld_H_q975 = NA_real_,            # Lambda* quantiles (log-HR scale)
  fld_H_nout = NA_integer_, fld_H_nin_mean = NA_real_,     # draw-usage counts (outer used; mean inner used)
  fld_H_secs = NA_real_,                                   # field block's own wall (timing_seconds)
  fld_H_note = NA_character_,                              # degenerate-case note (< 2 usable outer draws)
  # Uniform (kappa) calibration block (field_uniform = TRUE; else all NA).
  # lo2u/hi2u are the kappa*-widened two-sided interval on the HR scale.
  fld_H_kappa = NA_real_, fld_H_M = NA_integer_, fld_H_mass = NA_real_,
  fld_H_minC1 = NA_real_, fld_H_lo2u = NA_real_, fld_H_hi2u = NA_real_,
  fld_H_kappa_mcse = NA_real_, fld_H_uniform_secs = NA_real_,
  mr_harm_flag = NA_integer_, ij_source = NA_character_,
  sens = NA_real_, spec = NA_real_, ppv = NA_real_, npv = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

record_replicate <- function(sim_id) {
  rec <- .na_record(sim_id)

  df <- tryCatch(
    simulate_from_dgm(dgm, n = n_sample, analysis_time = analysis_time,
                      cens_adjust = cens_adjust, seed = seed_base + sim_id),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df)) { rec$status <- "CONFIG-ERROR"; return(rec) }
  df[[id_name]] <- seq_len(nrow(df))
  
  confs <- intersect(confounders_base, names(df))

# Add k_random_noise standard-normal noise covariates
# (k_random_noise is set upstream, e.g. in the setup chunk; 0 = no noise)
if (k_random_noise > 0) {
  noise_names <- paste0("noise", seq_len(k_random_noise))
  # Seed the noise draws by sim_id (offset to stay disjoint from the DGM seed
  # seed_base + sim_id) so the FULL replicate -- survival data AND noise -- is a
  # deterministic function of sim_id, independent of batch and loop position.
  # Without this the noise would draw from future's per-iteration RNG stream,
  # which is keyed to loop position, not sim_id, and could collide across batches.
  set.seed(seed_base + sim_id + 1000000L)
  for (nm in noise_names) {
    df[[nm]] <- rnorm(n = nrow(df))
  }
  confs <- c(confs, noise_names)
}
  
  
  rec$n_true <- sum(df[[harm_col]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)   # true |Q| this trial (all reps)

  
  # ---- Identification + naive + MR (single forestsearch call) -----
  # Args common to every method, plus a method-specific block.  Consistency-only
  # tuning (LASSO/two-stage/forced cuts/maxk) is NOT forwarded to DINA/GRF, which
  # have their own candidate enumeration; all methods search the same confs.
  base_args <- list(
    df.analysis     = df,
    outcome.name    = outcome_name, event.name = event_name,
    treat.name      = treat_name,   id.name    = id_name,
    flag_harm.name  = harm_col,     confounders.name = confs,
    is.RCT          = TRUE,         seedit = seed_base + sim_id,
    quiet           = TRUE,         # suppress per-fit console output
    sg_focus        = sg_focus,
    subgroup_method = subgroup_method,
    hr.threshold    = hr_threshold, hr.consistency = hr_consistency,
    pconsistency.threshold = pconsistency, n.min = n_min,
    selection_rule  = selection_rule,   # governs *MaxSG/*MinSG band (search, and MR's de-biasing family)
    effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,  # band width; inert unless the focus is effMaxSG/effMinSG
    stop_threshold  = stop_threshold,   # see @sec-setup; NULL, i.e. no early stopping
    parallel_args   = inner_parallel,              # parallel_mode: sims->sequential, boots->multisession
    mr_inference     = TRUE,
    mr_inference_args = mr_inference_args   # reselection derived from sg_focus
  )
  method_args <- switch(
    subgroup_method,
    consistency = list(
      consistency_method = consistency_method,
      use_lasso = use_lasso, use_grf = use_grf, use_twostage = use_twostage,
      use_dina = use_dina,
      conf_force = fs_conf_force, conf.cont_jcuts = fs_conf.cont_jcuts,
      fs.splits = fs_splits, maxk = maxk, d0.min = d0_min, d1.min = d1_min),
    dina = list(dina_select_statistic = dina_select_statistic,
                dina_args             = dina_args),
    grf  = list(grf_selection = grf_selection, grf_depth = grf_depth,
                dmin.grf = dmin.grf, grf_select_statistic = grf_select_statistic),
    stop("unknown subgroup_method: ", subgroup_method)
  )

  mr_t0 <- proc.time()[3]
  fs.est <- tryCatch(do.call(forestsearch, c(base_args, method_args)),
                     error = function(e) {
                       if (isTRUE(get0("diag_mode", ifnotfound = FALSE)))
                         warning(sprintf("FS-ERR sim %d: %s", sim_id,
                                         conditionMessage(e)), call. = FALSE)
                       NULL
                     })
  rec$fit_mr_secs <- proc.time()[3] - mr_t0   # forestsearch fit INCLUDING MR
  if (is.null(fs.est)) { rec$status <- "CONFIG-ERROR"; return(rec) }

  # Detection is METHOD-AGNOSTIC (a subgroup was identified), independent of
  # whether the MR produced a CI; MR availability is tracked
  # separately in mr_ok so an MR failure never masks a true detection.
  g     <- fs.est$mr_inference
  found <- !is.null(fs.est$sg.harm)
  rec$detected <- as.integer(found)
  if (found) {
    rec$sg_def <- paste(fs.est$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")          # full rule -> beta(Hhat) scoring
    rec$covs   <- paste(rule_covs(fs.est$sg.harm), collapse = "+")  # variable names -> id figures
  }
  if (!found) { rec$status <- "NO-DETECTION"; return(rec) }
  rec$status <- "DETECTED"
  rec$mr_ok <- as.integer(!is.null(g))

  if (!is.null(g)) {
    rec$label <- g$selected_label %||% NA_character_
    rec$n_sel <- g$n_selected      %||% NA_integer_
    # THREE-VALUED, deliberately.  `harm_flag` is NA when MR ran but bailed
    # before it could compute one (fs_mr_inference.R:391), and the package's own
    # documentation is explicit that NA here is "absence of evidence, not
    # evidence against harm" -- it warns against isTRUE(), which collapses NA to
    # FALSE and reports "harm not confirmed" for an analysis that never ran.
    # The previous as.integer(isTRUE(.)) did exactly that, so those replicates
    # entered the "MR flags harm in x%" denominator as zeros and biased it DOWN.
    # Keeping NA lets na.rm = TRUE drop them, which is what that figure means.
    rec$mr_harm_flag <- if (is.null(g$harm_flag) || is.na(g$harm_flag))
      NA_integer_ else as.integer(isTRUE(g$harm_flag))
    rec$ij_source    <- g$debiased$ij_source %||% NA_character_
    rec$nv_H_est <- g$naive$est;    rec$nv_H_lo <- g$naive$lower;    rec$nv_H_hi <- g$naive$upper;    rec$nv_H_se <- g$debiased$se_wald %||% NA_real_
    rec$mr_H_est <- g$debiased$est; rec$mr_H_lo <- g$debiased$lower; rec$mr_H_hi <- g$debiased$upper
    rec$mr_H_se_ij <- g$debiased$se_ij %||% NA_real_
    if (is.list(g$complement) && !is.null(g$complement$debiased)) {
      rec$nv_Hc_est <- g$complement$naive$est
      rec$nv_Hc_lo  <- g$complement$naive$lower
      rec$nv_Hc_hi  <- g$complement$naive$upper
      rec$nv_Hc_se  <- g$complement$debiased$se_wald %||% NA_real_
      rec$mr_Hc_est <- g$complement$debiased$est
      rec$mr_Hc_lo  <- g$complement$debiased$lower
      rec$mr_Hc_hi  <- g$complement$debiased$upper
      rec$mr_Hc_se_ij <- g$complement$debiased$se_ij %||% NA_real_
    }
    # ---- MR (field) block (ci_method = "field"; Hhat only, decision F3) ----
    # g$field is absent under ci_method "ij"/"wald" and degenerates to a bare
    # `note` when fewer than 2 outer draws were usable; both cases leave the
    # numeric fld_H_* columns NA and (for the latter) record the note.
    if (is.list(g$field)) {
      f <- g$field
      rec$fld_H_note <- f$note %||% NA_character_
      if (is.null(f$note)) {
        rec$fld_H_est2     <- f$est2
        rec$fld_H_lo2s     <- f$lower_2s;  rec$fld_H_hi2s <- f$upper_2s
        rec$fld_H_lo1s     <- f$lower_1s
        rec$fld_H_lo_se    <- f$lower_se;  rec$fld_H_hi_se <- f$upper_se
        rec$fld_H_se       <- f$se_field
        rec$fld_H_lam_mean <- f$lambda_mean
        rec$fld_H_q05  <- f$q05;  rec$fld_H_q25  <- f$q25;  rec$fld_H_q50 <- f$q50
        rec$fld_H_q75  <- f$q75;  rec$fld_H_q95  <- f$q95
        rec$fld_H_q025 <- f$q025; rec$fld_H_q975 <- f$q975
        rec$fld_H_nin_mean <- f$n_in_used_mean
        rec$fld_H_secs     <- f$timing_seconds %||% NA_real_
        # Uniform block (field_uniform = TRUE; absent or note-carrying -> NA).
        if (is.list(f$uniform) && is.null(f$uniform$note)) {
          u <- f$uniform
          rec$fld_H_kappa        <- u$kappa
          rec$fld_H_M            <- u$M
          rec$fld_H_mass         <- u$mass_covered
          rec$fld_H_minC1        <- u$minC1
          rec$fld_H_lo2u         <- u$lower_2u
          rec$fld_H_hi2u         <- u$upper_2u
          rec$fld_H_kappa_mcse   <- u$kappa_mcse
          rec$fld_H_uniform_secs <- u$timing_seconds
        }
      }
      rec$fld_H_nout <- f$n_out_used %||% NA_integer_
    }
  }

  # ---- Classification of Ĥ against the true harm flag ----------------------
  cl <- .classify(fs.est$grp.consistency$sg.harm.id, df[[harm_col]])
  rec$sens <- cl["sens"]; rec$spec <- cl["spec"]
  rec$ppv  <- cl["ppv"];  rec$npv <- cl["npv"]
  rec$n_harm <- sum(fs.est$grp.consistency$sg.harm.id == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

  # ---- FB bootstrap (H2 = León Eq.7) -----------------------------------
  # forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture re-runs whichever engine fs.est used (via
  # fs.est$args_call_all), regenerating the candidate family on each resample.
  # For "consistency" the family is fixed, so FB and the MR target
  # the same estimand; for "dina"/"grf" the family regenerates per resample, so
  # FB is the *unconditional* comparator against MR's
  # *conditional-on-family* estimate -- a FB<->MR gap there is the
  # family-regeneration signal, not an error.  If an engine cannot return H2 the
  # call falls back to NULL (fb_* stay NA) and the message is captured in fb_err.
  if (run_fb && subgroup_method %in% c("consistency", "dina", "grf")) {
    fb_t0 <- proc.time()[3]; fb_err <- NA_character_
    boot <- tryCatch(
      forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
        fs.est, nb_boots = nb_boots, seed = seed_base + sim_id,
        parallel_args = inner_parallel,
        # Pinned to the package default, purely so the setting is visible.
        # It is a no-op: FALSE is the formal default
        # (bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:193) and bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:597
        # strips mr_inference from the replicate call regardless, so the
        # un-pinned call already took this path.  Setting TRUE would run MR
        # inside every replicate and attach an mr_replicates payload that
        # nothing here consumes.
        mr_in_replicates = FALSE),
      error = function(e) { fb_err <<- conditionMessage(e); NULL })
    rec$fb_secs <- proc.time()[3] - fb_t0
    rec$fb_err  <- fb_err
    if (!is.null(boot) && !is.null(boot$H_estimates)) {
      he <- boot$H_estimates                     # H2 = León Eq.7 (both bias sources)
      # %||% guards a missing H2 column (get_dfRes omits H2 when the 2nd-order
      # bias adjustment is unavailable): a bare NULL assignment would DELETE the
      # column from rec, and the resulting short record ABORTS THE WHOLE BATCH.
      # Not a silent drop -- rbind() on data.frames with differing columns
      # errors ("numbers of columns of arguments do not match"), and neither
      # run-loop path survives it: "boots" mode combines with
      # do.call(rbind, lapply(...)), and in "sims" mode the failure is in
      # foreach's .combine, which .errorhandling = "remove" does not cover
      # (that only removes errors raised in the loop BODY).  One malformed
      # replicate therefore loses the entire run, not one cell.
      rec$fb_H_est <- he$H2 %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_H_lo  <- he$H2_lower %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_H_hi  <- he$H2_upper %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_H_se  <- .se_beta_hr(he$sdH2 %||% NA_real_, he$H2 %||% NA_real_)
    }
    if (!is.null(boot) && !is.null(boot$Hc_estimates)) {
      hce <- boot$Hc_estimates
      rec$fb_Hc_est <- hce$H2 %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_Hc_lo  <- hce$H2_lower %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_Hc_hi  <- hce$H2_upper %||% NA_real_
      rec$fb_Hc_se  <- .se_beta_hr(hce$sdH2 %||% NA_real_, hce$H2 %||% NA_real_)
    }
  }

  # ---- Oracle: refit on the TRUE harm subgroup of this trial ---------------
  oH  <- .cox_hr_ci(df[df[[harm_col]] == 1, , drop = FALSE])
  oHc <- .cox_hr_ci(df[df[[harm_col]] == 0, , drop = FALSE])
  rec$or_H_est <- oH["est"];   rec$or_H_lo <- oH["lo"];   rec$or_H_hi <- oH["hi"];   rec$or_H_se <- oH["se"]
  rec$or_Hc_est <- oHc["est"]; rec$or_Hc_lo <- oHc["lo"]; rec$or_Hc_hi <- oHc["hi"]; rec$or_Hc_se <- oHc["se"]

  rec
}

# Replicate-level error firewall.  record_replicate() guards the forestsearch()
# and simulate_from_dgm() calls internally, but everything else in its body --
# notably the base_args/method_args construction -- runs unguarded, so a setup
# mistake (an undefined knob, a bad argument name) escapes as an error from the
# replicate itself.  Both run paths DISCARDED such a replicate silently
# (.errorhandling = "remove"; the outer tryCatch), so an all-replicate config
# failure produced results = NULL and read downstream as "no detections".
# Returning the NA record WITH the message keeps the row -- and the reason -- in
# the bundle.  Mirrors the md40 harness's CONFIG-ERROR / NO-DETECTION /
# DETECTED trichotomy: a configuration failure must never read as a
# scientific null.
.safe_record <- function(s) {
  tryCatch(record_replicate(s), error = function(e) {
    rec <- .na_record(s); rec$err_msg <- conditionMessage(e)
    rec$status <- "CONFIG-ERROR"; rec
  })
}
```

# Run the simulation

```{r run-loop, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
results <- NULL
elapsed <- NA_real_   # combine mode has no wall-clock; NA -> em-dash in the timing table

if (run_smoke && identical(run_mode, "batch")) {
  sim_ids <- sim_id_start:(sim_id_start + n_sims - 1L)
  if (isTRUE(diag_mode)) sim_ids <- utils::head(sim_ids, 5L)  # diag cap (not a combinable batch)

  if (identical(parallel_mode, "sims")) {
    # replicates fan out across workers; each replicate's search + bootstrap are sequential
    plan("sequential"); gc()
    plan("multisession", workers = n_workers)

    t_all <- proc.time()[3]
    results <- foreach(
      s = sim_ids,
      .combine = rbind, .errorhandling = "remove",
      .options.future = list(packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table"),
                             seed = TRUE)
    ) %dofuture% {
      .safe_record(s)   # keeps a failed replicate (with its message) as a row
    }
    elapsed <- proc.time()[3] - t_all

    plan("sequential"); gc()   # release workers between phases
  } else {
    # "boots": replicates run sequentially in the main process; the forestsearch
    # search and the nb_boots bootstrap fan out over n_workers WITHIN each replicate
    # (via inner_parallel).  No outer pool -> no nested parallelism.
    plan("sequential"); gc()
    t_all <- proc.time()[3]
    results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sim_ids, .safe_record))
    elapsed <- proc.time()[3] - t_all
    plan("sequential"); gc()
  }

  # ---- Guard: the run loop must have produced a usable results frame --------
  # Without this, an all-replicate failure leaves results = NULL, and the very
  # next call (fs_attach_betaHhat) hits its `is.null(results$sg_def)` branch and
  # assigns into NULL -- which R COERCES TO A LIST.  `results` then looks
  # non-NULL to every `!is.null(results)` chunk guard downstream, and the first
  # 2-D subset (results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]) fails with
  # "incorrect number of dimensions" -- ~400 lines from the actual cause.
  # Fail here instead, naming the real reason.
  if (!is.data.frame(results) || !nrow(results))
    stop(sprintf("run loop produced no usable records for sim_id %d-%d.",
                 min(sim_ids), max(sim_ids)), call. = FALSE)
  .cfg_err <- unique(stats::na.omit(results$err_msg))
  if (length(.cfg_err) && all(!is.na(results$err_msg)))
    stop("CONFIG ERROR -- every replicate failed before any search ran.\n",
         "Distinct message(s):\n",
         paste0("  - ", .cfg_err, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  if (length(.cfg_err))
    warning(sprintf("%d of %d replicate(s) failed: %s", sum(!is.na(results$err_msg)),
                    nrow(results), paste(.cfg_err, collapse = " | ")), call. = FALSE)

  # ---- INVARIANT: every interval must satisfy lo <= hi ------------------------
  # Added after an inverted oracle interval reached a rendered table undetected.
  # A swapped pair is not visibly wrong in the record -- it surfaces only as a
  # negative mean CI length and coverage identically 0, several layers
  # downstream. This checks every estimator/block pair at the source.
  .ci_check <- function(r) {
    bad <- character(0)
    for (k in c("or","nv","fb","mr")) for (sfx in c("H","Hc")) {
      lo <- r[[paste0(k, "_", sfx, "_lo")]]; hi <- r[[paste0(k, "_", sfx, "_hi")]]
      if (is.null(lo) || is.null(hi)) next
      ok <- is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
      if (any(ok & hi < lo))
        bad <- c(bad, sprintf("%s_%s (%d of %d rows inverted)", k, sfx,
                              sum(ok & hi < lo), sum(ok)))
    }
    # Field intervals obey the same invariant: the quantile interval AND the
    # SE-type interval (both to_eff()'d, so monotone-transform safe).
    for (pr in list(c("fld_H_lo2s", "fld_H_hi2s"), c("fld_H_lo_se", "fld_H_hi_se"),
                    c("fld_H_lo2u", "fld_H_hi2u"))) {
      lo <- r[[pr[1]]]; hi <- r[[pr[2]]]
      if (is.null(lo) || is.null(hi)) next
      ok <- is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
      if (any(ok & hi < lo))
        bad <- c(bad, sprintf("%s/%s (%d of %d rows inverted)", pr[1], pr[2],
                              sum(ok & hi < lo), sum(ok)))
    }
    if (length(bad))
      stop("interval invariant violated -- hi < lo for: ",
           paste(bad, collapse = "; "),
           "\n  A swapped pair yields negative CI length and zero coverage; ",
           "fix the assignment before reading any table.", call. = FALSE)
    invisible(TRUE)
  }
  .ci_check(results)

  # Conditional truth targets beta(Hhat)/beta(Hhat^c) for the realized rule of each
  # detected replicate -- deduplicated over distinct sg_def, computed in the main
  # process so the large eval frame stays in one place (not copied into workers).
  # API ALIGNMENT: attach_betaHhat() -> fs_attach_betaHhat(), which now REQUIRES
  # an explicit `focus` (the harm/benefit convention is stated at the call site,
  # no default) and dispatches on `outcome_type`.  This is a harm-subgroup
  # design, so focus = "harm".  Same dedup-over-sg_def semantics; it adds
  # betaHhat_H/betaHhat_Hc (read downstream) plus betaHhat_status/nH_eval/
  # nHc_eval.  Undetected rows (sg_def = NA) take the no-subgroup record (whole
  # frame is the complement) instead of dropping out.
  results <- fs_attach_betaHhat(results, eval_df, focus = "harm",
                                outcome_type = "survival",
                                outcome.name = outcome_name,
                                event.name = event_name,
                                treat.name = treat_name)

  # ---- fb_mode = "join": adopt FB columns from the committed bundle ---------
  # FB is JOINED, never recomputed (task protocol; decision F5).  Columns fb_*
  # are copied by sim_id from the committed bundle; sim_ids outside it stay NA
  # and are thereby RECORDED as FB-absent.  The join is licensed per replicate
  # by the naive-estimate identity (same data, same selection): any joined,
  # detected row whose nv_H_est differs beyond 1e-12 relative is a hard stop.
  if (identical(fb_mode, "join")) {
    if (!file.exists(fb_join_path))
      stop("fb_mode = 'join': committed FB bundle not found at ", fb_join_path)
    .fbb <- readRDS(fb_join_path)$results
    .idx <- match(results$sim_id, .fbb$sim_id)          # NA -> outside the bundle
    # Gate 2 amendment: enumerated flip replicates are excluded from the join
    # BEFORE any copy -- their fb_* stay NA (FB-absent) -- and both selections
    # are printed so the exclusion is self-documenting in the render.
    .skip <- intersect(fb_join_skip, results$sim_id[!is.na(.idx)])
    for (s in .skip)
      cat(sprintf("FB join: sim %d SKIPPED per join_skip (cross-vintage selection flip) -- committed selection [%s] vs this run [%s]; recorded FB-absent.\n",
                  s, .fbb$sg_def[.fbb$sim_id == s], results$sg_def[results$sim_id == s]))
    .idx[results$sim_id %in% fb_join_skip] <- NA_integer_
    .hit <- which(!is.na(.idx))
    for (cc in c("fb_H_est","fb_H_lo","fb_H_hi","fb_H_se",
                 "fb_Hc_est","fb_Hc_lo","fb_Hc_hi","fb_Hc_se",
                 "fb_secs","fb_err"))
      results[[cc]][.hit] <- .fbb[[cc]][.idx[.hit]]
    .chk <- .hit[results$detected[.hit] %in% 1L]
    .rd  <- abs(results$nv_H_est[.chk] - .fbb$nv_H_est[.idx[.chk]]) /
            pmax(abs(.fbb$nv_H_est[.idx[.chk]]), .Machine$double.eps)
    if (length(.chk) && any(is.finite(.rd) & .rd > 1e-12))
      stop(sprintf("fb_mode = 'join': naive-estimate identity FAILED on %d of %d joined detected rows (max rel diff %.3e) -- the FB bundle does not describe these replicates.",
                   sum(.rd > 1e-12, na.rm = TRUE), length(.chk), max(.rd, na.rm = TRUE)))
    cat(sprintf("FB join: %d of %d sim_ids matched %s (%d detected, naive identity max rel diff %s); %d sim_ids FB-absent.\n",
                length(.hit), nrow(results), basename(fb_join_path), length(.chk),
                if (length(.chk)) sprintf("%.2e", max(c(0, .rd), na.rm = TRUE)) else "n/a",
                nrow(results) - length(.hit)))
  }

  cat(sprintf("Batch sim_id %d-%d: %d/%d detections in %.1f s (%.1f s/replicate).\n",
              min(sim_ids), max(sim_ids),
              sum(results$detected, na.rm = TRUE), length(sim_ids), elapsed,
              elapsed / max(1L, length(sim_ids))))
  # Status trichotomy, printed so a CONFIG-ERROR run can never be mistaken for
  # a low-detection one: those two produce the SAME `detected` count.
  print(knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = results$status,
                                         useNA = "ifany")),
                     caption = "Replicate status."))
  if (run_fb) {
    cat(sprintf("Mean wall-clock: fit+MR %.3f s vs FB bootstrap %.2f s (B=%d).\n",
                mean(results$fit_mr_secs, na.rm = TRUE),
                mean(results$fb_secs, na.rm = TRUE), nb_boots))

    # Surface any (otherwise-swallowed) FB bootstrap error(s) on detected reps.
    fb_tried <- sum(results$detected == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)
    fb_fail  <- sum(results$detected == 1L & is.na(results$fb_H_est), na.rm = TRUE)
    if (fb_fail > 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("FB bootstrap returned no estimate on %d of %d detected replicate(s).\n",
                  fb_fail, fb_tried))
      errs <- unique(stats::na.omit(results$fb_err))
      if (length(errs))
        cat("Distinct FB error(s):\n", paste0("  - ", errs, collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
    }
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("Mean wall-clock: fit+MR %.3f s  (FB skipped: nb_boots = %s).\n",
                mean(results$fit_mr_secs, na.rm = TRUE),
                if (is.null(nb_boots)) "NULL" else as.character(nb_boots)))
  }

  # Persist the results bundle (knob in @sec-setup).  Saved as a list so the
  # truth targets and key counts travel with the per-replicate records, and the
  # tables can be regenerated downstream without re-running the simulation.
  if (isTRUE(save_rds) && !is.null(results)) {
    dir.create(dirname(rds_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    saveRDS(list(results = results, truth = truth,
                 meta = list(n_sample = n_sample, n_sims = n_sims,
                             nb_boots = nb_boots, mr_draws = mr_draws,
                             subgroup_method = subgroup_method,
                             sim_id_start = sim_id_start, sim_id_end = sim_id_end,
                             seed_base = seed_base, parallel_mode = parallel_mode,
                             # --- provenance, RECORD ONLY -------------------
                             # Deliberately NOT added to the agreement-check key
                             # vector in combine mode: a missing field resolves
                             # to NA there and NA counts as a distinct value, so
                             # every batch written before this change would
                             # stop() the pool.  These exist so a bundle can be
                             # identified after the fact -- which identifier,
                             # which build, how many workers -- not to gate
                             # anything.
                             sg_focus            = sg_focus,
                             focus_tag           = focus_tag,
                             consistency_method  = consistency_method,
                             # --- template provenance (fb_mr_field) ---------
                             ci_method           = mr_ci_method,
                             field_uniform       = mr_field_uniform,
                             fb_mode             = fb_mode,
                             fb_join_source      = if (identical(fb_mode, "join"))
                                                     basename(fb_join_path) else NA_character_,
                             fb_join_skip        = if (identical(fb_mode, "join"))
                                                     paste(fb_join_skip, collapse = ",") else NA_character_,
                             campaign_tag        = campaign_tag,
                             target_hr_harm      = target_hr_harm,
                             field_R             = "R_out=1000/R_in=500 (package defaults; not forwarded by forestsearch())",
                             stop_threshold      = paste(deparse(stop_threshold),
                                                         collapse = " "),
                             selection_rule      = selection_rule,
                             effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,
                             forestsearch_version =
                               as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")),
                             n_workers           = n_workers,
                             r_version           = as.character(getRversion()),
                             hostname            = unname(Sys.info()[["nodename"]]),
                             built_at            = Sys.time())),
            rds_path)
    cat(sprintf("Saved batch bundle (%d rows, sim_id %d-%d) to %s\n",
                nrow(results), sim_id_start, sim_id_end, rds_path))
  }

} else if (run_smoke && identical(run_mode, "combine")) {
  # ---- Combine seed-disjoint batches into one pooled results set -----------
  # Reads every ..._res_*.rds (or the explicit `combine_files`), validates that
  # the batches are poolable, refuses on overlapping sim_id, and populates the
  # same globals (`results`, `truth`, `n_sims`, ...) the report chunks consume --
  # so every downstream table renders on the union with no other change.
  files <- if (!is.null(combine_files)) combine_files else Sys.glob(combine_glob)
  files <- files[file.exists(files)]
  if (!length(files))
    stop("combine mode: no batch files found (combine_glob = '", combine_glob, "').")

  bundles <- lapply(files, readRDS)

  # Count-invariant meta MUST agree across batches to pool them.
  .meta_get <- function(b, k) b$meta[[k]] %||% NA
  # Template bundles always carry ci_method / campaign_tag / target_hr_harm
  # (batch save above), so they join the poolability gate: batches from a
  # different campaign or ci_method must never silently pool.  fb_mode is
  # deliberately NOT gated -- one campaign legitimately mixes "join" (the
  # committed FB range) with "none" (beyond it).
  for (k in c("n_sample", "nb_boots", "mr_draws", "subgroup_method", "seed_base",
              "ci_method", "campaign_tag", "target_hr_harm")) {
    vals <- unique(lapply(bundles, .meta_get, k = k))
    if (length(vals) > 1L)
      stop(sprintf("combine mode: batches disagree on meta$%s (%s).",
                   k, paste(unlist(vals), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # truth must match across batches (same DGM + seed_base); use the first.
  truths <- lapply(bundles, `[[`, "truth")
  if (length(truths) > 1L &&
      !all(vapply(truths[-1], identical, logical(1), truths[[1]])))
    warning("combine mode: truth targets differ across batches; using the first.")
  truth <- truths[[1]]

  # Pool the per-replicate records.
  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(bundles, `[[`, "results"))

  # Disjointness: a repeated sim_id means the seed ranges overlapped, so the
  # pooled set is NOT independent -- refuse rather than silently double-count.
  dup <- unique(results$sim_id[duplicated(results$sim_id)])
  if (length(dup))
    stop(sprintf("combine mode: %d duplicated sim_id across batches (e.g. %s); seed ranges overlap.",
                 length(dup), paste(utils::head(sort(dup), 5L), collapse = ", ")))

  # Make the report self-describing from the files (not the setup chunk's knobs).
  n_sample        <- bundles[[1]]$meta$n_sample        %||% n_sample
  nb_boots        <- bundles[[1]]$meta$nb_boots        %||% nb_boots
  mr_draws      <- bundles[[1]]$meta$mr_draws      %||% mr_draws
  subgroup_method <- bundles[[1]]$meta$subgroup_method %||% subgroup_method
  run_fb       <- is.numeric(nb_boots) && length(nb_boots) == 1L && nb_boots >= 1L
  n_sims          <- sum(vapply(bundles,
                                function(b) as.integer(b$meta$n_sims %||% NA_integer_),
                                integer(1)))

  rng <- range(results$sim_id)
  cat(sprintf("Combined %d batch file(s) -> %d rows, sim_id %d-%d (n_sims = %d).\n",
              length(files), nrow(results), rng[1], rng[2], n_sims))
  cat("  files: ", paste(basename(files), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

  # Persist the pooled bundle so downstream docs load ONE file.  The name is
  # chosen to fall OUTSIDE combine_glob ("..._res_*"), so a later re-combine never
  # re-ingests this pooled file alongside the batch pieces.
  if (isTRUE(save_combined)) {
    cpath <- combined_path %||%
      file.path("results", sprintf("%s_combined_%d_%d.rds", rds_stem, rng[1], rng[2]))
    dir.create(dirname(cpath), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    saveRDS(list(results = results, truth = truth,
                 meta = list(n_sample = n_sample, n_sims = n_sims,
                             nb_boots = nb_boots, mr_draws = mr_draws,
                             subgroup_method = subgroup_method,
                             sim_id_start = rng[1], sim_id_end = rng[2],
                             seed_base = bundles[[1]]$meta$seed_base %||% NA_integer_,
                             n_batches = length(files),
                             source_files = basename(files),
                             # Provenance carried from the first pooled bundle,
                             # as seed_base already is.  NA for batches written
                             # before provenance was recorded.
                             sg_focus   = bundles[[1]]$meta$sg_focus %||% NA_character_,
                             focus_tag  = bundles[[1]]$meta$focus_tag %||% NA_character_,
                             ci_method  = bundles[[1]]$meta$ci_method %||% NA_character_,
                             campaign_tag = bundles[[1]]$meta$campaign_tag %||% NA_character_,
                             target_hr_harm = bundles[[1]]$meta$target_hr_harm %||% NA_real_,
                             fb_mode_by_batch = vapply(bundles, function(b)
                               b$meta$fb_mode %||% NA_character_, character(1)),
                             fb_join_skip_by_batch = vapply(bundles, function(b)
                               b$meta$fb_join_skip %||% NA_character_, character(1)),
                             consistency_method =
                               bundles[[1]]$meta$consistency_method %||% NA_character_,
                             stop_threshold =
                               bundles[[1]]$meta$stop_threshold %||% NA_character_,
                             forestsearch_version =
                               bundles[[1]]$meta$forestsearch_version %||% NA_character_)),
            cpath)
    cat(sprintf("Saved pooled bundle (%d rows, sim_id %d-%d, %d batches) to %s\n",
                nrow(results), rng[1], rng[2], length(files), cpath))
  }
}
```
