# Timing and scale-up projection

MR cost per replicate is essentially fixed (one fit + the multiplier draws,
independent of `nb_boots`); FB cost scales **linearly** with `nb_boots`
(it re-runs the whole search once per bootstrap). The projection below uses the
measured per-replicate times and assumes FB runs only on detected
replicates. The modelled wall-clock spreads the reps over the workers respecting
the integer reps-per-worker ceiling, then a single calibration factor (measured
wall / modelled wall on this run) carries this run's realized overhead into the
projections.

```{r timing-distributions}
# PORTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN: the per-replicate cost DISTRIBUTION, not just
# the mean the projection below consumes.  A long right tail on fb_secs is the
# signature of a few replicates whose resamples nearly all detect.
.dist_row <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return(rep(NA_real_, 14))
  c(min = min(x), stats::quantile(x, probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1)),
    median = stats::median(x), mean = mean(x), max = max(x), n = length(x))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(fit_mr_secs = .dist_row(results$fit_mr_secs),
                   fb_secs     = .dist_row(results$fb_secs)),
  digits = 2,
  caption = sprintf("Per-replicate seconds (all replicates; %s mode, %d workers).",
                    parallel_mode, n_workers))
.tl <- rbind(data.frame(component = "fit + MR",     secs = results$fit_mr_secs),
             data.frame(component = "FB bootstrap", secs = results$fb_secs))
.tl <- .tl[is.finite(.tl$secs), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(.tl)) {
  ggplot(.tl, aes(x = component, y = secs)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.6) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Seconds per replicate", title = "Per-replicate wall costs") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}
```

```{r timing-projection}
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  # NB: the whole forestsearch() call -- the search PLUS MR -- which is the
  # cost FB is then measured on top of.  MR's own cost alone is in
  # fs.est$mr_inference$timing_seconds.
  mr_mean  <- mean(results$fit_mr_secs, na.rm = TRUE)          # forestsearch fit + MR, per rep
  det_rate <- mean(results$detected, na.rm = TRUE)
  # FB timing only when FB actually ran; nb_boots may be 0L or NULL.
  boots_disp <- if (run_fb) as.integer(nb_boots) else 0L
  fb_mean  <- if (run_fb) mean(results$fb_secs, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  per_boot <- if (run_fb && boots_disp > 0L) fb_mean / boots_disp else NA_real_

  fmt_hm <- function(sec) {
    if (!is.finite(sec)) return("\u2014")                       # no timing available
    h <- floor(sec / 3600); m <- round((sec - 3600 * h) / 60)
    if (h >= 1) sprintf("%d h %02d m", h, m) else sprintf("%d m", round(sec / 60))
  }

  # Per-rep total cost (MR every rep; FB on the det_rate fraction only).
  per_rep_total <- function(B) {
    fb_rep <- if (run_fb && is.finite(per_boot)) per_boot * B else 0
    mr_mean + det_rate * fb_rep
  }
  # Modelled wall-clock, by parallel_mode:
  #  "sims"  -> replicates fan out, so the busiest worker handles ceil(ns/n_workers)
  #             reps and sets the wall (the integer ceiling matters at smoke-test
  #             scale, where ns can be < n_workers).
  #  "boots" -> replicates run sequentially, so the wall is their sum (ns * per-rep);
  #             the parallelism is already inside per_rep_total via the measured
  #             (parallel) bootstrap time.
  wall_model <- function(ns, B) {
    if (identical(parallel_mode, "boots")) ns * per_rep_total(B)
    else ceiling(ns / n_workers) * per_rep_total(B)
  }

  # Calibration: the busiest-worker model still omits load imbalance, per-rep
  # variance, and fixed overhead (pool spin-up, gc, dispatch, DGM build, table
  # render).  In BATCH mode we have a measured wall clock, so calibrate ONE
  # multiplier k = elapsed / wall_model(current run) and apply it to every
  # projection: by construction the current-run calibrated wall equals the
  # measured wall, and projections inherit this run's realized overhead.  In
  # COMBINE mode there is no single wall clock, so k is undefined and the
  # calibrated column is left blank.
  wall_model_cur <- wall_model(n_sims, boots_disp)
  k_cal <- if (is.finite(elapsed) && is.finite(wall_model_cur) && wall_model_cur > 0)
             elapsed / wall_model_cur else NA_real_

  proj_row <- function(ns, B, actual_sec = NA_real_) {
    fb_rep  <- if (run_fb && is.finite(per_boot)) per_boot * B else NA_real_
    cpu_sec <- ns * per_rep_total(B)                           # total serial CPU-seconds
    w_model <- wall_model(ns, B)                               # busiest-worker idealization
    w_cal   <- if (is.finite(k_cal)) k_cal * w_model else NA_real_
    data.frame(n_sims = ns, B = as.integer(B),
               mr_rep_s = round(mr_mean, 1),
               fb_rep_s = if (is.finite(fb_rep)) round(fb_rep, 0) else NA_real_,
               cpu_hours = round(cpu_sec / 3600, 1),
               wall_actual = fmt_hm(actual_sec),
               wall_model  = fmt_hm(w_model),
               wall_cal    = fmt_hm(w_cal),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  cur <- proj_row(n_sims, boots_disp, actual_sec = elapsed)
  scn <- do.call(rbind, lapply(proj_scenarios,
                               function(s) proj_row(s[["n_sims"]], s[["nb_boots"]])))
  tab <- rbind(cbind(Scenario = "current run", cur),
               cbind(Scenario = "projection",  scn))

  run_label <- if (is.finite(elapsed))
    sprintf("%d reps in %.0f s on %d workers", n_sims, elapsed, n_workers)
  else
    sprintf("%d reps pooled from batch files (no single wall-clock)", n_sims)
  if (run_fb) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Current run: %s. Per rep: fit+MR %.1f s, FB %.0f s (B=%d, ~%.1f s/bootstrap). Detection %.0f%%.\n",
      run_label, mr_mean, fb_mean, boots_disp, per_boot, 100 * det_rate))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Current run: %s. Per rep: fit+MR %.1f s (FB skipped). Detection %.0f%%.\n",
      run_label, mr_mean, 100 * det_rate))
  }
  if (is.finite(k_cal))
    cat(sprintf("Realized overhead factor k = %.2f (measured wall / busiest-worker model).\n", k_cal))

  gt(tab) |>
    tab_header(title = "Wall-clock projection",
               subtitle = sprintf("%s mode \u00b7 %d workers \u00b7 detection %.0f%%%s",
                                  parallel_mode, n_workers, 100 * det_rate,
                                  if (is.finite(k_cal)) sprintf(" \u00b7 k = %.2f", k_cal) else "")) |>
    cols_label(n_sims = "sims", B = "boots", mr_rep_s = "fit+MR/rep (s)",
               fb_rep_s = "FB/rep (s)", cpu_hours = "CPU-hours",
               wall_actual = "wall (actual)",
               wall_model = "wall (modeled)", wall_cal = "wall (calibrated)") |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "`wall (actual)` is the **measured** wall-clock for the current run",
      "(\u2014 for projections, and in combine mode, which have no single wall-clock).",
      if (identical(parallel_mode, "boots"))
        "`wall (modeled)` = sims \u00d7 per-rep cost (replicates sequential; the bootstrap parallelizes inside each), where per-rep cost ="
      else
        "`wall (modeled)` = ceil(sims / workers) \u00d7 per-rep cost (replicates parallel, bootstrap sequential), where per-rep cost =",
      if (run_fb)
        "fit+MR/rep + detection \u00d7 FB/rep (FB/rep = per-bootstrap cost \u00d7 boots);"
      else
        "fit+MR/rep (FB skipped);",
      "It omits load imbalance and fixed overhead.",
      "`wall (calibrated)` = k \u00d7 modeled, with k = measured wall / modeled wall on THIS run,",
      "so the current row reproduces the measured wall and projections carry this run's realized overhead.",
      "`CPU-hours` = sims \u00d7 per-rep cost (total serial work).")))
}
```

# Subgroup sizes

```{r subgroup-size-callout, results='asis'}
#| code-fold: true
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  rH <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  nH <- rH$n_harm[is.finite(rH$n_harm)]
  if (length(nH)) {
    nHc <- n_sample - nH
    .fmt <- function(v) sprintf(
      "mean %.0f (SD %.0f), range [%d, %d], %.1f%% of ITT",
      mean(v), stats::sd(v), as.integer(min(v)), as.integer(max(v)),
      100 * mean(v) / n_sample)
    has_true <- "n_true" %in% names(rH) && any(is.finite(rH$n_true))

    cat(sprintf(
      "\n::: {.callout-note title=\"Identified subgroup sizes (%d of %d replicates detected, N = %d each)\"}\n\n",
      nrow(rH), nrow(results), n_sample))
    cat(sprintf("- **Harm $\\widehat H$**: %s\n", .fmt(nH)))
    cat(sprintf("- **Complement $\\widehat H^{c}$**: %s\n", .fmt(nHc)))
    if (has_true) {
      nT <- rH$n_true[is.finite(rH$n_true)]
      cat(sprintf("- **True harm $Q$**: %s\n", .fmt(nT)))
      cat(sprintf(
        "\nThe identified $\\widehat H$ averages **%.1f%%** of ITT against a true harm prevalence of **%.1f%%**; this small-subgroup regime is what stresses the large-sample behaviour of the MR.\n",
        100 * mean(nH) / n_sample, 100 * mean(nT) / n_sample))
    } else {
      cat(sprintf(
        "\nThe identified $\\widehat H$ averages **%.1f%%** of ITT (the true harm subgroup is ~11%% of ITT by design); this small-subgroup regime is what stresses the large-sample behaviour of the MR.\n",
        100 * mean(nH) / n_sample))
    }
    cat("\n:::\n\n")
  } else {
    cat("\n::: {.callout-note title=\"Identified subgroup sizes\"}\nNo subgroup was identified on any replicate, so no $\\widehat H$ sizes are available.\n:::\n\n")
  }
}
```

# Estimation / coverage table (León Table 2 layout + MR)

```{r estimation-table}
# All summaries are finite-only: non-finite estimates/bounds (e.g. from Cox
# separation or an unstable small-B IJ) are dropped so a single blow-up cannot
# dominate a mean.
.cover <- function(target, lo, hi) {
  target <- rep_len(target, length(lo))   # recycle scalar targets (CDE/marginal) to n reps
  ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(target[ok] >= lo[ok] & target[ok] <= hi[ok])
}
.pbias <- function(est, target) {
  d <- (est - target) / target; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
  if (!length(d)) return(NA_real_)
  100 * mean(d)
}
.mfin <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_ }
.sdfin <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x) > 1L) sd(x) else NA_real_ }
# Empirical (true) SD on the log-HR (beta) scale: SD of log(HR) across reps.
.sd_log <- function(e) { l <- log(e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]); if (length(l) > 1L) sd(l) else NA_real_ }
# Stored per-replicate log-HR (beta-scale) SE for an estimator -- read at the
# source, never back-calculated from CI bounds (or_/nv_/fb_*_se; MR uses its IJ
# SE, mr_*_se_ij).  A missing column (results saved before SEs were stored)
# yields all-NA so the table still renders.
.get_se <- function(r, k, suffix) {
  col <- if (k == "fld") "fld_H_se"
         else if (k == "mr") paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_se_ij")
         else paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_se")
  v <- r[[col]]
  if (is.null(v)) rep(NA_real_, nrow(r)) else v
}

# Estimator rows for one block.  FB appears whenever fb_* data exist (run OR
# joined); MR (field) appears in the Hhat block only (decision F3 -- the gate
# computes no complement field) and uses est2 with the two-sided quantile
# interval as its primary interval (decision F4).
est_keys_for <- function(r, suffix) {
  keys <- c(oracle = "or", naive = "nv", FB = "fb",
            `MR (IJ)` = "mr", `MR (field)` = "fld")
  if (!any(is.finite(r$fb_H_est))) keys <- keys[names(keys) != "FB"]
  if (!identical(suffix, "H") || !any(is.finite(r$fld_H_est2)))
    keys <- keys[names(keys) != "MR (field)"]
  keys
}
.est_cols <- function(r, k, suffix) {
  if (k == "fld") list(e = r$fld_H_est2, lo = r$fld_H_lo2s, hi = r$fld_H_hi2s)
  else list(e  = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_est")]],
            lo = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_lo")]],
            hi = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_hi")]])
}

# Build one block (H or Hc): estimator rows against the four targets.
build_block <- function(r, suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
  est_keys <- est_keys_for(r, suffix)
  or_est <- r[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]   # per-replicate oracle target
  bH_est <- r[[paste0("betaHhat_", suffix)]]     # per-replicate beta(Hhat) target
  rows <- lapply(names(est_keys), function(lab) {
    k  <- est_keys[[lab]]
    ec <- .est_cols(r, k, suffix)
    e  <- ec$e
    lo <- ec$lo
    hi <- ec$hi
    len <- hi - lo; len <- len[is.finite(len)]
    seb <- .get_se(r, k, suffix)                  # stored log-HR (beta) SE
    data.frame(
      Estimator = lab,
      n       = sum(is.finite(e)),
      Avg     = .mfin(e),
      SD        = .sd_log(e),                      # empirical SD, log-HR (beta) scale  [reported]
      SD_hr     = .sdfin(e),                       # empirical SD, HR scale             [retained]
      SD_hat    = .mfin(seb),                      # mean model SE, log-HR (beta) scale [reported]
      SD_hat_hr = .mfin(e * seb),                  # mean model SE, HR scale            [retained]
      Length  = if (length(len)) mean(len) else NA_real_,
      b_oracle = .pbias(e, or_est),
      b_betaHhat = .pbias(e, bH_est),
      b_cde    = .pbias(e, tgt_cde),
      b_marg   = .pbias(e, tgt_marg),
      Cov_oracle = .cover(or_est, lo, hi),
      Cov_betaHhat = .cover(bH_est, lo, hi),
      Cov_cde    = .cover(tgt_cde,  lo, hi),
      Cov_marg   = .cover(tgt_marg, lo, hi),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  # FB rows render whenever fb_* data exist -- computed (fb_mode "run") or
  # adopted from the committed bundle (fb_mode "join").  run_fb alone cannot
  # gate this: it is FALSE under "join".
  fb_in_tables <- any(is.finite(results$fb_H_est))
  rH  <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  blockH  <- build_block(rH, "H",  truth$cde_H,  truth$marg_H)
  blockHc <- build_block(rH, "Hc", truth$cde_Hc, truth$marg_Hc)
  # Fold the mean identified subgroup size into the block label, so |H-hat|
  # travels with the table (as in build_estimation_table()'s row-group labels).
  .blk_lab <- function(label, sym, v) {
    if (!any(is.finite(v))) return(label)
    sprintf("%s (mean |%s| = %.0f, %.1f%% ITT)", label, sym,
            mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), 100 * mean(v, na.rm = TRUE) / n_sample)
  }
  est_tab <- rbind(
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Harm  \u0124", "\u0124", rH$n_harm), blockH),
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Complement  \u0124\u1d9c", "\u0124\u1d9c",
                           n_sample - rH$n_harm), blockHc)
  )

  det_rate <- mean(results$detected, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Classification + decision + IJ-stability diagnostics (over detected reps).
  cls <- sprintf("sens %.2f \u00b7 spec %.2f \u00b7 PPV %.2f \u00b7 NPV %.2f",
                 .mfin(rH$sens), .mfin(rH$spec), .mfin(rH$ppv), .mfin(rH$npv))
  # MR availability: the share of DETECTED reps for which MR returned an object.
  # The detected-only denominator is what makes this mean "MR failed" rather than
  # "nothing was found": .na_record() sets mr_ok = 0L, so every undetected rep
  # also carries mr_ok = 0 and an unconditional mean would just reproduce the
  # detection rate.  Reported because mr_ok is otherwise invisible -- a run where
  # MR failed on a third of the detected reps would read identically to one where
  # it never failed.
  mr_avail  <- mean(rH$mr_ok, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Both of the following are ALREADY conditional on MR having run: mr_harm_flag
  # and ij_source stay NA when g is NULL, and na.rm = TRUE drops those reps.  So
  # their denominator is mr_avail * |detected|, not |detected| -- which is why
  # availability is stated first and these two read "among those".
  harm_rate <- mean(rH$mr_harm_flag, na.rm = TRUE)
  ij_ok     <- mean(rH$ij_source == "ij", na.rm = TRUE)

  gt(est_tab, groupname_col = "Block") |>
    tab_header(
      title = if (fb_in_tables)
        "FB vs MR (IJ) vs MR (field): estimation & coverage"
      else "MR (IJ) vs MR (field): estimation & coverage",
      subtitle = sprintf("hr=%.2f \u00b7 n=%d, %d sims, draws=%d \u00b7 fb_mode=%s \u00b7 resample identification",
                         target_hr_harm, n_sample, n_sims, mr_draws, fb_mode)) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Avg, SD, SD_hr, SD_hat, SD_hat_hr, Length), decimals = 2) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg), decimals = 1) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg), decimals = 2) |>
    cols_label(
      n = "n",
      SD = md("$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$"), SD_hat = md("$\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$"),
      b_oracle = md("$b^{\\text{or}}$"), b_betaHhat = md("$b^{\\beta}$"),
      b_cde = md("$b^{\\ddagger}$"), b_marg = md("$b^{\\dagger}$"),
      Cov_oracle = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\text{or}}$"), Cov_betaHhat = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\beta}$"),
      Cov_cde = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\ddagger}$"), Cov_marg = md("$C^{\\dagger}$")) |>
    cols_hide(columns = c(SD_hr, SD_hat_hr)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Relative bias (%)", columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "95% coverage", columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg)) |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(sprintf(
      "Detection rate **%.0f%%** of %d sims; MR returned an estimate on **%.0f%%** of detected reps; among those, MR flags harm in **%.0f%%** and IJ variance held (not fallback) in **%.0f%%**. Classification of \u0124 vs true subgroup: %s. Summaries finite-only over detected reps; `n` = finite reps contributing.",
      100 * det_rate, n_sims, 100 * mr_avail, 100 * harm_rate, 100 * ij_ok, cls))) |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$ (empirical SD) and $\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$ (mean of the model SEs) are on the log-hazard-ratio ($\\beta$) scale; HR-scale versions are computed but hidden.",
      "Targets: $b^{\\text{or}}$ vs per-replicate oracle $\\hat\\theta(H)$;",
      "$b^{\\beta}$ / $\\hat C^{\\beta}$ vs the conditional subgroup HR $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ at the realized region (Theorem 2 target);",
      "$b^{\\ddagger}$ vs CDE $\\theta^{\\ddagger}$;",
      "$b^{\\dagger}$ vs marginal subgroup HR $\\theta^{\\dagger}$.",
      "`Length` = mean CI length.",
      if (fb_in_tables)
        "FB = `H2` (León Eq.7, both bias sources); MR (IJ) = de-biased estimate with IJ interval; MR (field) = shrunk-field `est2` with the two-sided 95% Lambda-quantile interval (its SE column is the Lambda-SD `se_field`). The field is computed for the Hhat block only (F3); Hhat-c stays on the IJ interval."
      else
        "MR (IJ) = de-biased estimate with IJ interval; MR (field) = shrunk-field `est2` with the two-sided 95% Lambda-quantile interval (its SE column is the Lambda-SD `se_field`); field is Hhat-block only (F3). FB absent in this cell/range.")))
}
```

The table below is a **median** companion to the table above, over the same
detected replicates and rendered identically so the columns line up. Location
columns (point estimate, $\widehat{\text{SD}}$, CI length, relative bias) use the
median; **SD**, **n**, and coverage are computed exactly as above.

```{r estimation-table-medians}
# Median companion to the main (mean-based) table, rendered the SAME way -- a
# single auto-printed gt -- so the column formatting matches exactly.  Reuses
# .cover()/.sdfin() from the estimation-table chunk; location columns use the
# median.  The mean "Length" column is dropped (Len(med) already gives it).
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {

  .medfin     <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x)) stats::median(x) else NA_real_ }
  .pbias_med  <- function(est, target) {
    d <- (est - target) / target; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
    if (!length(d)) return(NA_real_)
    100 * stats::median(d)
  }

  build_block_med <- function(r, suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
    est_keys <- est_keys_for(r, suffix)   # same roster as the mean table
    or_est <- r[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]
    bH_est <- r[[paste0("betaHhat_", suffix)]]
    rows <- lapply(names(est_keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- est_keys[[lab]]
      ec <- .est_cols(r, k, suffix)
      e  <- ec$e
      lo <- ec$lo
      hi <- ec$hi
      len <- hi - lo; len <- len[is.finite(len)]
      seb <- .get_se(r, k, suffix)                  # stored log-HR (beta) SE
      data.frame(
        Estimator = lab,
        n       = sum(is.finite(e)),
        Med     = .medfin(e),
        SD        = .sd_log(e),                      # empirical SD, log-HR (beta) scale  [reported]
        SD_hr     = .sdfin(e),                       # empirical SD, HR scale             [retained]
        SD_hat    = .medfin(seb),                    # median model SE, log-HR (beta)     [reported]
        SD_hat_hr = .medfin(e * seb),                # median model SE, HR scale          [retained]
        Length  = if (length(len)) stats::median(len) else NA_real_,
        b_oracle = .pbias_med(e, or_est),
        b_betaHhat = .pbias_med(e, bH_est),
        b_cde    = .pbias_med(e, tgt_cde),
        b_marg   = .pbias_med(e, tgt_marg),
        Cov_oracle = .cover(or_est, lo, hi),
        Cov_betaHhat = .cover(bH_est, lo, hi),
        Cov_cde    = .cover(tgt_cde,  lo, hi),
        Cov_marg   = .cover(tgt_marg, lo, hi),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
    do.call(rbind, rows)
  }

  rHm <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  est_tab_med <- rbind(
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Harm  \u0124", "\u0124", rHm$n_harm),
          build_block_med(rHm, "H",  truth$cde_H,  truth$marg_H)),
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Complement  \u0124\u1d9c", "\u0124\u1d9c",
                           n_sample - rHm$n_harm),
          build_block_med(rHm, "Hc", truth$cde_Hc, truth$marg_Hc))
  )

  gt(est_tab_med, groupname_col = "Block") |>
    tab_header(
      title = "Median summary (companion to the table above)",
      subtitle = sprintf("Same detected reps \u00b7 hr=%.2f, n=%d, %d sims, draws=%d \u00b7 location columns are medians",
                         target_hr_harm, n_sample, n_sims, mr_draws)) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Med, SD, SD_hr, SD_hat, SD_hat_hr, Length), decimals = 2) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg), decimals = 1) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg), decimals = 2) |>
    cols_label(
      n = "n", Med = "Median",
      SD = md("$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$"), SD_hat = md("$\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$"),
      b_oracle = md("$b^{\\text{or}}$"), b_betaHhat = md("$b^{\\beta}$"),
      b_cde = md("$b^{\\ddagger}$"), b_marg = md("$b^{\\dagger}$"),
      Cov_oracle = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\text{or}}$"), Cov_betaHhat = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\beta}$"),
      Cov_cde = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\ddagger}$"), Cov_marg = md("$C^{\\dagger}$")) |>
    cols_hide(columns = c(SD_hr, SD_hat_hr)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Relative bias (%)", columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "95% coverage", columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg)) |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "Median counterpart to the mean-based table above, over the same detected reps.",
      "Point estimate (**Median**), $\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$, `Len(med)`, and relative bias are medians;",
      "$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$, **n**, and all **coverage** rates are computed exactly as above.",
      "$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$ and $\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$ are on the log-hazard-ratio scale.",
      "Estimator conventions as in the mean table (FB = `H2`; MR (field) = `est2` with the quantile interval, Hhat block only).")))
}
```

# The conditional target $\beta(\widehat H)$ vs the oracle

```{r betaHhat-callout, results='asis'}
#| code-fold: true
# Narrative companion to the estimation tables: summarises the new conditional
# target beta(Hhat) and contrasts it with the oracle.  Pure consumer of `results`
# (no simulation), reusing the table's per-replicate relative-bias / coverage
# logic, restricted to the harm block where the contrast lives.
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  rC <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  ok <- is.finite(rC$betaHhat_H)
  if (any(ok)) {
    .relb <- function(est, tgt) { d <- (est - tgt) / tgt; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
                                  if (length(d)) 100 * mean(d) else NA_real_ }
    .covg <- function(tgt, lo, hi) { o <- is.finite(tgt) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
                                     if (any(o)) 100 * mean(tgt[o] >= lo[o] & tgt[o] <= hi[o]) else NA_real_ }
    bH  <- rC$betaHhat_H        # realized-region truth (the Theorem 2 target)
    orH <- rC$or_H_est         # oracle: effect at the TRUE region (theta-dagger(H))
    keys <- c(naive = "nv", FB = "fb", MR = "mr")
    if (!run_fb) keys <- keys[names(keys) != "FB"]
    erows <- vapply(names(keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- keys[[lab]]
      e  <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_est")]]; lo <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_lo")]]; hi <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_hi")]]
      sprintf("| %s | %.2f | %+.0f%% | %+.0f%% | %.0f%% | %.0f%% |",
              lab, mean(e[is.finite(e)]), .relb(e, bH), .relb(e, orH),
              .covg(bH, lo, hi), .covg(orH, lo, hi))
    }, character(1))
    mr_m   <- mean(rC$mr_H_est[is.finite(rC$mr_H_est)])
    nearer <- if (isTRUE(abs(mr_m - mean(orH, na.rm = TRUE)) <= abs(mr_m - mean(bH))))
                "the oracle (true-region) effect $\\theta^{\\dagger}(H)$" else "$\\beta(\\widehat H)$"

    cat(sprintf("\n::: {.callout-note title=\"The \u03b2(\u0124) target vs the oracle \u2014 harm block, %d detections\"}\n\n", sum(ok)))
    cat("$\\beta(\\widehat H)$ is the population value of the standard within-subgroup analysis ",
        "(the Cox hazard ratio of treatment) at the **realized** region $\\widehat H$ \u2014 the truth of the ",
        "subgroup the search actually found, and the conditional estimand Theorem 2 certifies. It is a ",
        "*per-replicate* target. The **oracle** $\\hat\\theta(H)$ refits on the **true** region $H$ instead ",
        "(the effect one would estimate knowing the subgroup); their gap is the price of selecting the ",
        "wrong region.\n\n", sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("- $\\beta(\\widehat H)$: mean **%.2f** (median %.2f)  \u00b7  $\\beta(\\widehat H^{c})$: mean %.2f\n",
                mean(bH), stats::median(bH), mean(rC$betaHhat_Hc[is.finite(rC$betaHhat_Hc)])))
    cat(sprintf("- oracle $\\hat\\theta(H)$: mean **%.2f**  (true-region effect $\\theta^{\\dagger}(H) = %.2f$)\n",
                mean(orH, na.rm = TRUE), truth$marg_H))
    cat(sprintf("- discovery gap $\\hat\\theta(H) - \\beta(\\widehat H)$: mean **%.2f**\n\n",
                mean((orH - bH)[is.finite(orH - bH)])))
    cat("| estimator | mean | bias vs $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ | bias vs oracle | cov $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ | cov oracle |\n")
    cat("|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n")
    cat(paste(erows, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
    cat(sprintf("In this cell the MR estimate sits nearer %s. ", nearer))
    cat("The *bias vs $\\beta(\\widehat H)$* column is what Theorem 2 speaks to; *bias vs oracle* is distance ",
        "from the true-region effect. ", sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("At %d detections these figures are indicative, not a coverage read.\n", sum(ok)))
    cat("\n:::\n\n")
  }
}
```

# Paired FB ↔ MR agreement panel {#sec-paired}

For a fixed candidate family (`consistency`) both procedures correct the *same*
selected $\hat H$ on the *same* data, so per-replicate differences isolate the
`dfbeta` linearisation -- the cleanest test of the leading-order correspondence.
For `dina`/`grf` the FB bootstrap regenerates the family (and re-selects) on
each resample while MR holds the observed family fixed, so the differences
additionally carry the family-regeneration gap (unconditional vs
conditional-on-family). Reported on the log-effect scale.

```{r paired-panel, results='asis'}
# Runs whenever fb_* data exist -- computed (fb_mode "run") or joined from the
# committed bundle (fb_mode "join"); run_fb alone cannot gate it.
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && any(is.finite(results$fb_H_est))) {
  rd <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]

  # Per-block log-scale agreement (comparator - FB) on point estimate and
  # bounds.  mr_cols selects the comparator: the MR (IJ) columns, or the
  # MR (field) est2 with its quantile interval (task 1a: the agreement panel
  # gains est2; field exists for the Hhat block only, F3).
  agree_block <- function(suffix, mr_cols = c("mr_%s_est", "mr_%s_lo", "mr_%s_hi"),
                          comparator = "MR (IJ)") {
    e1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_est")]]; e2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[1], suffix)]]
    l1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_lo")]];  l2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[2], suffix)]]
    u1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_hi")]];  u2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[3], suffix)]]
    ok <- is.finite(e1) & is.finite(e2)
    if (sum(ok) < 2L) return(NULL)
    blk <- sprintf("%s \u00b7 %s",
                   if (suffix == "H") "Harm \u0124" else "Complement \u0124\u1d9c",
                   comparator)
    dpt <- log(e2[ok]) - log(e1[ok])
    dlo <- log(l2[ok]) - log(l1[ok]); dhi <- log(u2[ok]) - log(u1[ok])
    list(
      tab = data.frame(
        Block = blk,
        Quantity = c("log point", "log CI lower", "log CI upper"),
        mean_d = c(mean(dpt), .mfin(dlo), .mfin(dhi)),
        sd_d   = c(sd(dpt),   .sdfin(dlo), .sdfin(dhi)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      n = sum(ok), corr = suppressWarnings(cor(log(e1[ok]), log(e2[ok]))),
      pts = data.frame(block = blk, fb = e1[ok], mr = e2[ok])
    )
  }

  aH  <- agree_block("H"); aHc <- agree_block("Hc")
  aHf <- agree_block("H", mr_cols = c("fld_%s_est2", "fld_%s_lo2s", "fld_%s_hi2s"),
                     comparator = "MR (field) est2")
  parts <- Filter(Negate(is.null), list(aH, aHc, aHf))

  if (length(parts)) {
    tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "tab"))
    sub <- paste(vapply(parts, function(p)
      sprintf("%s: %d reps, corr %.3f", p$tab$Block[1], p$n, p$corr),
      character(1)), collapse = "  \u00b7  ")
    cat(as_raw_html(
      gt(tab, groupname_col = "Block") |>
        tab_header(title = "MR \u2212 FB (log scale)", subtitle = sub) |>
        cols_label(mean_d = "Mean \u0394", sd_d = "SD \u0394") |>
        fmt_number(columns = c(mean_d, sd_d), decimals = 4)
    ))

    pts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "pts"))
    p <- ggplot(pts, aes(x = fb, y = mr)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
      geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
      facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free") +
      labs(x = expression("FB  "*hat(theta)^"*"),
           y = expression("MR  "*tilde(theta)),
           title = "Per-replicate de-biased point estimates") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    print(p)
  } else {
    cat("Too few paired replicates at smoke-test counts to draw the panel.\n")
  }
}
```

# MR (field) diagnostics {#sec-field}

The field-calibrated interval's own summaries (task
`TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05`, Stage 3 layout): two-sided 95% coverage
with Wilson intervals (the paper's primary convention, F4), one-sided lower
coverage as the supplementary read, retained bias of the de-biased estimate
$\tilde\beta$ and the shrunk-field `est2` against the conditional target
$\beta(\widehat H)$ (log-HR and SD units), the $\lambda$-SD/SD calibration
ratio, and the Monte Carlo draw-usage counts.

```{r field-coverage-wilson}
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && any(is.finite(results$fld_H_est2))) {
  rF <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]

  # Wilson 95% interval for a coverage proportion (paper convention).
  .wilson <- function(x, n, z = qnorm(0.975)) {
    if (!is.finite(x) || !is.finite(n) || n <= 0) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    ctr <- (x + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
    hw  <- z * sqrt(x * (1 - x) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
    c(ctr - hw, ctr + hw)
  }
  .cov_n <- function(target, lo, hi) {           # coverage + its denominator
    target <- rep_len(target, length(lo))
    ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
    if (!any(ok)) return(c(NA_real_, 0L))
    c(mean(target[ok] >= lo[ok] & target[ok] <= hi[ok]), sum(ok))
  }
  .cov1_n <- function(target, lo1s) {            # one-sided: target >= lower bound
    target <- rep_len(target, length(lo1s))
    ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(lo1s)
    if (!any(ok)) return(c(NA_real_, 0L))
    c(mean(target[ok] >= lo1s[ok]), sum(ok))
  }
  z95 <- qnorm(0.95)

  cov_rows <- function(suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
    keys <- est_keys_for(rF, suffix)
    or_est <- rF[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]
    bH_est <- rF[[paste0("betaHhat_", suffix)]]
    tgt <- list(oracle = or_est, betaHhat = bH_est, cde = tgt_cde, marg = tgt_marg)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- keys[[lab]]
      ec <- .est_cols(rF, k, suffix)
      # One-sided 95% lower bound: the field stores its own (lambda q95); the
      # normal-based estimators derive exp(log est - z95 * se_beta) -- the
      # same construction as their two-sided bounds, so this is a convention,
      # not a new model.  Documented as the supplementary read (F4).
      lo1s <- if (k == "fld") rF$fld_H_lo1s
              else { seb <- .get_se(rF, k, suffix)
                     ifelse(is.finite(ec$e) & is.finite(seb) & ec$e > 0,
                            exp(log(ec$e) - z95 * seb), NA_real_) }
      do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tgt), function(tn) {
        c2 <- .cov_n(tgt[[tn]], ec$lo, ec$hi)
        w  <- .wilson(c2[1], c2[2])
        c1 <- .cov1_n(tgt[[tn]], lo1s)
        data.frame(Block = if (suffix == "H") "Harm Ĥ" else "Complement Ĥᶜ",
                   Estimator = lab, Target = tn,
                   n = as.integer(c2[2]), Cov2s = c2[1],
                   W_lo = w[1], W_hi = w[2], Cov1s = c1[1],
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }))
    }))
  }
  cw <- rbind(cov_rows("H",  truth$cde_H,  truth$marg_H),
              cov_rows("Hc", truth$cde_Hc, truth$marg_Hc))
  gt(cw, groupname_col = "Block") |>
    tab_header(title = "95% coverage with Wilson intervals (two-sided primary; one-sided supplementary)",
               subtitle = "Targets: per-replicate oracle; beta(Hhat) (conditional, primary); CDE; marginal") |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov2s, W_lo, W_hi, Cov1s), decimals = 3) |>
    cols_label(Cov2s = "2-sided cov", W_lo = "Wilson lo", W_hi = "Wilson hi",
               Cov1s = "1-sided cov") |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "Wilson interval on the two-sided coverage proportion (paper convention, primary; F4).",
      "One-sided coverage = share of replicates with target >= the 95% lower bound:",
      "the field row uses its stored `lower_1s` (lambda q95 inversion); the normal-based rows use exp(log est - 1.645 se).")))
}
```

```{r field-bias-coverage}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.6
# Bias-vs-coverage display for THIS cell (TASK_bias_coverage_display_2026-09-06):
# one point per estimator against the Gaussian bookkeeping reference.  The

  bc <- fs_sim_bias_coverage(results, block = "H", estimators = c("mr", "fld"))
  bc$cell <- sprintf("hr=%.2f, n=%d%s", target_hr_harm, n_sample,
```

```{r field-retained-bias}
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && any(is.finite(results$fld_H_est2))) {
  rF <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  ok <- is.finite(rF$betaHhat_H) & rF$betaHhat_H > 0

  .ret <- function(est) {                        # retained bias vs beta(Hhat), log scale
    d <- log(est[ok]) - log(rF$betaHhat_H[ok]); d <- d[is.finite(d)]
    c(mean = mean(d), sd_est = stats::sd(d), n = length(d))
  }
  rb_mr  <- .ret(rF$mr_H_est)
  rb_fld <- .ret(rF$fld_H_est2)
  rb_nv  <- .ret(rF$nv_H_est)

  # lambda-SD / SD: mean model-side lambda SD over the empirical SD of est2
  # (both log scale) -- the field's SE calibration ratio.
  sd_emp_fld <- .sd_log(rF$fld_H_est2)
  sd_emp_mr  <- .sd_log(rF$mr_H_est)
  lam_ratio  <- .mfin(rF$fld_H_se) / sd_emp_fld
  ij_ratio   <- .mfin(rF$mr_H_se_ij) / sd_emp_mr

  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    quantity = c("naive retained bias vs beta(Hhat)  [log-HR]",
                 "MR (IJ) retained bias vs beta(Hhat)  [log-HR]",
                 "MR (field) est2 retained bias vs beta(Hhat)  [log-HR]",
                 "MR (IJ) retained bias  [SD units]",
                 "MR (field) est2 retained bias  [SD units]",
                 "IJ SE / empirical SD  (MR (IJ))",
                 "lambda-SD / empirical SD  (MR (field))"),
    value = c(rb_nv["mean"], rb_mr["mean"], rb_fld["mean"],
              rb_mr["mean"] / sd_emp_mr, rb_fld["mean"] / sd_emp_fld,
              ij_ratio, lam_ratio),
    n = c(rb_nv["n"], rb_mr["n"], rb_fld["n"], rb_mr["n"], rb_fld["n"],
          NA, NA)),
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Retained bias against the conditional target beta(Hhat) (harm block), and SE-calibration ratios (log-HR scale).")

  # Draw-usage + field cost diagnostics.
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    metric = c("outer draws used (mean / min, of R_out = 1000)",
               "inner draws used per outer (mean, of R_in = 500)",
               "field block seconds (mean / median)",
               "replicates with a degenerate field (note set)"),
    value = c(sprintf("%.1f / %d", .mfin(rF$fld_H_nout), suppressWarnings(min(rF$fld_H_nout, na.rm = TRUE))),
              sprintf("%.1f", .mfin(rF$fld_H_nin_mean)),
              sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", .mfin(rF$fld_H_secs), .medfin(rF$fld_H_secs)),
              sprintf("%d of %d detected", sum(!is.na(rF$fld_H_note)), nrow(rF)))),
    caption = "MR (field) Monte Carlo draw usage and cost (detected replicates).")
}
```

# Identification structure {#sec-identification}

The supplement's identification summary (its Figures/Table "FS identification
structure"), computed here on this run rather than assembled separately. The
engine is `fs_identification_summary()` in the package, so this document, the
continuous twin, and the manuscript fragments all share one implementation.

Each detected replicate's realized rule is classified against the planted
triple: the **anchor** `er`, its true binary **partner** `meno`, and the
correlated continuous **proxy** `age` that may substitute for the partner. The
near-tie between $\{\mathrm{er} \cap \mathrm{meno}\}$ and its `age` proxy is the
phenomenon these summaries exist to expose.

```{r identification-structure}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Sweep points are supplied as a NAMED list; a single batch has one point.  The
# manuscript figures pass two or more (n = 500, 1000, ...) and the same call
# draws the trend.  Bundles may be given as in-memory frames (as here) or as
# paths to saved .rds files.
#
# Classification keys on `sg_def`, so this works whether or not `covs` was
# populated -- the GLM/continuous harness leaves `covs` empty by design, and
# reading it directly would classify every replicate as "anchor missed".
id_run <- fs_identification_summary(
  bundles = stats::setNames(list(results), as.character(n_sample)),
  anchor  = "er",     # the factor FS recovers as the trial grows
  partner = "meno",   # the true binary partner
  proxy   = "age",    # correlated continuous covariate FS may substitute
  confounders = confounders_base,
  sweep_label = "Trial size (n)")
id_run
```

```{r identification-involvement}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| message: false
plot_fs_identification_involvement(id_run)
```

```{r identification-composition}

#| fig-height: 4.2
#| message: false

```

```{r identification-table}
#| message: false
```

```{r identification-block}
# PORTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN: classification accuracy as a TABLE.  The
# estimation-table footnote already carries the means; this adds the medians and
# makes the numbers findable rather than buried in a footnote string.
.rI <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(.rI)) {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    metric = c("sens", "spec", "ppv", "npv"),
    mean   = c(.mfin(.rI$sens), .mfin(.rI$spec), .mfin(.rI$ppv), .mfin(.rI$npv)),
    median = c(.medfin(.rI$sens), .medfin(.rI$spec), .medfin(.rI$ppv), .medfin(.rI$npv))),
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Classification of the identified subgroup vs the true harm flag (detected reps).")
}
```

## Selected-covariate and covariate-pair frequencies

```{r identification-figures}
# PORTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN.  Complementary to the structure summary
# above: that classifies each rule into five categories, this shows the raw
# per-covariate selection shares over the whole analysis pool, plus the realized
# rules by frequency.
if (nrow(.rI)) {
  .cov_list <- lapply(.rI$sg_def, rule_covs)
  .cov_all  <- unique(unlist(.cov_list))
  if (length(.cov_all)) {
    .cf <- vapply(.cov_all, function(v)
      mean(vapply(.cov_list, function(x) v %in% x, logical(1))), numeric(1))
    .cf_df <- data.frame(covariate = names(.cf), share = unname(.cf))
    .cf_df$true_region <- .cf_df$covariate %in% c("er", "meno")
    print(
      ggplot(.cf_df, aes(x = reorder(covariate, share), y = share, fill = true_region)) +
        geom_col() + coord_flip() +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey60"),
                          labels = c(`TRUE` = "true-region covariate", `FALSE` = "other"),
                          name = NULL) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of detected replicates selecting the covariate",
             title = "Selected-covariate frequencies",
             subtitle = "True harm region: er <= 8 & meno == 0") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
    # COLLAPSED OVER CUT VALUES.  The raw rules-by-frequency table listed every
    # distinct `sg_def` string and was dominated by cut noise -- on a
    # 500-replicate survival run, 322 distinct rules over 346 detections, with
    # `{age <= 46} & {nodes <= 5}` and `{nodes <= 3} & {age <= 46}` as separate
    # rows despite being the same pairing.  fs_rule_covariate_pairs() sorts and
    # de-duplicates the covariate names, so orderings collapse together, as do
    # equivalent spellings of one condition (`!{meno}` vs `{meno == 0}`).  The
    # same run reduces to 22 signatures.
    #
    # `k` is the number of DISTINCT covariates, so a band on a single variable
    # (`!{nodes <= 3} & {nodes <= 5}`) shows as k = 1 rather than being hidden;
    # `n_rules` is how many distinct rule strings collapsed into the row.
    .pairs <- fs_rule_covariate_pairs(.rI, true_covariates = c("er", "meno"))
    print(plot_fs_rule_pairs(.rI, true_covariates = c("er", "meno"), top_n = 12L))
    knitr::kable(.pairs, digits = 3,
      caption = paste("Selected-covariate-pair frequencies: realized rules",
                      "collapsed over cut values, detected reps.",
                      "`k` = distinct covariates in the signature;",
                      "`n_rules` = distinct rule strings that collapsed into it."))
  }
}
```

# Notes for scale-up

* **Counts.** Move `n_sims` $\to$ 1000 $\to$ 20000 and `nb_boots` $\to$ 200–500
  in @sec-setup; nothing else changes. FB is the wall-clock bottleneck (the
  per-replicate timing line above quantifies the gap).
* **M2 / M3 and the regime sweep.** Add the smaller-$N$ / noise-factor cells
  (`n_add_noise`, $N \in \{500, 300\}$) and the true-HR $\times$ $n_S$ sweep once
  the M1 cell looks sane; the small-$n_S$ M3 cell is the linearisation's stress
  test.
* **FSlg.** Set `use_grf = TRUE` to match León's LASSO+GRF screening; the smoke
  test uses LASSO-only for speed.
* **Target semantics to confirm.** The three targets here are (per-replicate
  oracle, DGM `cde_H`/`cde_Hc`, DGM `hr_H_true`/`hr_Hc_true`). Before publishing
  numbers, confirm these match the $\theta^{\ddagger}$/$\theta^{\dagger}$
  definitions used by `build_estimation_table()` / León Table 5.

```{r session-info}
# Single, unambiguous start-to-finish wall-clock: from the first line of `setup`
# to here.  This is the true total cost of running the whole document -- setup +
# library loads + DGM build + every simulation replicate (MR AND FB
# bootstrap) + all table rendering -- not a per-rep mean or a model.
.fmt_dur <- function(s) {
  h <- s %/% 3600; m <- (s %% 3600) %/% 60; sec <- round(s %% 60)
  if (h >= 1) sprintf("%d h %02d m %02d s", h, m, sec)
  else if (m >= 1) sprintf("%d m %02d s", m, sec)
  else sprintf("%.1f s", s)
}
.secs_total <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t0_doc, units = "secs"))
cat(sprintf("TOTAL wall-clock, start to finish: %s  (= %.0f s; %d reps on %d workers)\n",
            .fmt_dur(.secs_total), .secs_total, n_sims, n_workers))

sessionInfo()
```
